3. Eslab qolish usuli

Har kuni 5 tadan fe'lni uchala shakli bilan ovoz chiqarib takrorlang: "go — went — gone".
tip: O'zbek tilida fe'l o'zagi o'zgarmaydi (bor-di, bor-gan). Inglizchada esa ko'p fe'llarning o'zi butunlay o'zgaradi (go → went → gone). Shuning uchun ularni jadval qilib yodlash eng yaxshi usul.
ex: I took a taxi to the airport.
English is spoken all over the world.
He broke his phone last week.

title: What are you doing tomorrow?
lesson:
Oldindan rejalashtirilgan, kelishilgan ishlar uchun am/is/are + -ing:

• What are you doing tomorrow?
(Ertaga nima qilyapsiz? / Ertaga rejangiz nima?)
• I'm meeting Ali on Friday.
(Juma kuni Ali bilan uchrashaman.)
• We're flying to Istanbul next week.
(Keyingi hafta Istanbulga uchamiz.)

Jadval (poyezd, film, dars) uchun present simple:
• The train leaves at 7.30.
(Poyezd 7:30 da jo'naydi.)

q.w: Ertangi reja haqida savol → are you doing.

q.q: She ___ to the dentist on Monday. (go)
q.uz: U dushanba kuni tish shifokoriga boradi.

q.w: Kelajakdagi reja haqida savol → Are you working?

q.q: What time ___ the film start tonight?
q.uz: Bugun kechqurun film soat nechada boshlanadi?

intro:
Bu mavzuda kelajak haqida gapirishning bir usulini o'rganamiz. Biz present continuous (am/is/are + -ing) ni oldindan rejalashtirilgan, kelishib qo'yilgan ishlar uchun ham ishlatamiz.

I'm meeting Ali tomorrow. (Ertaga Ali bilan uchrashaman — kelishib qo'yganmiz.)

Jadval bo'yicha bo'ladigan ishlar (poyezd, kino, dars) uchun esa present simple: The train leaves at 7.
explain:
1. Rejalar uchun present continuous

am / is / are + -ing + kelajak vaqti (tomorrow, on Friday, next week)
• What are you doing this evening? (Bugun kechqurun nima qilyapsiz? / rejangiz nima?)
• We're flying to Istanbul on Monday. (Dushanba kuni Istanbulga uchamiz.)
• She's getting married next month. (U keyingi oy turmushga chiqyapti.)
Odatda chipta olingan, uchrashuv belgilangan bo'ladi.

2. Jadval uchun present simple

Transport, kino, dars jadvali:
• The film starts at 8. (Film soat 8 da boshlanadi.)
• What time does the train leave? (Poyezd soat nechada jo'naydi?)

3. Solishtiring

I'm doing (reja)It starts (jadval)
I'm going to the cinema tonight.The film starts at 7.30.
Odam o'zi kelishganRasmiy jadval
tip: O'zbekchada kelajak uchun ham ko'pincha hozirgi zamon ishlatiladi: "Ertaga Samarqandga ketyapman". Inglizchada ham xuddi shunday: I'm going to Samarkand tomorrow.
ex: I'm meeting my friends on Saturday.
We're having a party next Friday.
mi: The train is leaving at 7.30 every day.
The train leaves at 7.30 every day.
I going to the dentist tomorrow.
I'm going to the dentist tomorrow.

title: I'm going to ...
lesson:
am/is/are going to + verb — niyat, qaror qilingan ish:
• I'm going to buy a new phone.
(Yangi telefon sotib olmoqchiman.)

Hozirgi belgilarga qarab bashorat:
• Look at the sky! It's going to rain.
(Osmonga qarang! Yomg'ir yog'adi.)

Negative: I'm not going to … · Question: Are you going to …?

q.q: I'm going ___ buy a new phone.
Look at those clouds! It ___ rain.
q.w: Bulutlar — belgi → is going to rain.

q.q: What ___ you going to do this weekend?
We ___ going to watch the match. We're tired. (negative)
He ___ going to sell his car.
I'm going to ___ my homework now. (do)

q.w: Belgi: yiqilish aniq → are going to.

intro:
Going to — kelajak haqida gapirishning yana bir usuli. Biz uni:
• niyat, qaror uchun ishlatamiz: I'm going to buy a car. (Mashina sotib olmoqchiman.)
• hozirgi belgilarga qarab bashorat uchun: Look at the clouds! It's going to rain. (Yomg'ir yog'adi.)

O'zbek tilida bunga ko'pincha "-moqchi" to'g'ri keladi: o'qimoqchiman, ketmoqchi.
explain:
1. Shakli

am / is / are + going to + fe'l (1-shakl)
Misol
+I'm going to study tonight.
−She isn't going to come.
?Are you going to buy it?
Savol so'ziWhat are you going to do?

2. Niyat (qaror qilib qo'yilgan)

• I'm going to learn French next year. (Keyingi yil fransuz tilini o'rganmoqchiman.)
• We're going to paint the kitchen. (Oshxonani bo'yamoqchimiz.)

3. Belgiga qarab bashorat

Hozir nimadir ko'rinib turibdi va natija aniq:
• Be careful! You're going to fall! (Ehtiyot bo'ling! Yiqilasiz!)
• She's going to have a baby. (U farzand ko'radi.)

4. Eslab qoling

going to dan keyin fe'l 1-shaklda: going to buy (not buying, bought).
tip: O'zbekchadagi "-moqchiman" (sotib olmoqchiman, o'qimoqchiman) ko'pincha I'm going to ga to'g'ri keladi.
ex: I'm going to visit my grandparents.
What are you going to do after school?
We aren't going to stay long.
It's 8.55. We're going to be late!
Look at that dark sky. It's going to rain.
Anavi qora osmonga qarang. Yomg'ir yog'adi.
mi: She's going to buys a car.
She's going to buy a car.

title: will / shall 1
lesson:
will + verb — kelajak haqida fikr, bashorat:
• I think it will rain tomorrow.
(Menimcha, ertaga yomg'ir yog'adi.)
• She'll be 20 next year.
(U keyingi yil 20 yoshga to'ladi.)

Negative: won't (will not) · Question: Will you …?
• I won't be at home tomorrow.
(Ertaga uyda bo'lmayman.)

q.q: Don't worry. The exam ___ be difficult. (negative)
Where ___ you be at 10 o'clock tomorrow?

intro:
Will — kelajak zamonini bildiradi. Biz uni kelajak haqidagi fikr, taxmin, bashorat uchun ishlatamiz: "Menimcha, u keladi", "Ertaga yomg'ir yog'adi".

O'zbek tilidagi "-adi" (kelajak ma'nosida) yoki "-ar" ga to'g'ri keladi: keladi, yutadi, bo'lar.
I think it will rain tomorrow. (Menimcha, ertaga yomg'ir yog'adi.)
explain:
1. Shakli

will + fe'l (1-shakl) — barcha shaxslar uchun bir xil.
To'liqQisqa
+I will goI'll go
−I will not goI won't go
?Will you go?—

2. Qachon ishlatiladi?

• Fikr, taxmin (I think, I'm sure, probably bilan): I think he'll pass the exam. (Menimcha, u imtihondan o'tadi.)
• Kelajakdagi fakt: She'll be 18 next year. (U keyingi yil 18 ga to'ladi.)
• Va'da: I won't tell anyone. (Hech kimga aytmayman.)

3. will yoki going to?

• going to — oldindan qilingan reja yoki ko'rinib turgan belgi
• will — fikr, taxmin, gapirayotgan paytda qilingan qaror (Unit 28)
• I think it will rain. (fikr) · Look at the clouds, it's going to rain. (belgi)

4. Eslab qoling

will dan keyin to yo'q va fe'lga -s qo'shilmaydi: He will go (not will goes, will to go).
tip: O'zbekchada kelajak ko'pincha "-adi" bilan aytiladi (ertaga keladi). Inglizchada esa hozirgi zamon emas, will kerak: He will come tomorrow.
ex: I think you'll like this film.
Don't worry. Everything will be OK.
I won't be at home tonight.
U, ehtimol, keyinroq sizga qo'ng'iroq qiladi.

title: will / shall 2
lesson:
Gapirayotgan paytda qaror qilsak — I'll:
• The phone is ringing. — I'll answer it.
(Telefon jiringlayapti. — Men ko'taraman.)
• I'm cold. — I'll close the window.
(Sovqotyapman. — Derazani yopaman.)

Taklif uchun Shall I / Shall we …?
• Shall I help you?
(Yordam beraymi?)
• Shall we go out tonight?
(Bugun kechqurun tashqariga chiqamizmi?)

q.q: The phone is ringing. — I ___ it.
I'm cold. — I ___ close the window.
___ I help you with your bag?
___ we go to the cinema tonight?
I'm hungry. — I ___ you a sandwich.
It's late. I think I ___ go home now.
q.uz: Kech bo'ldi. Menimcha, endi uyga boraman.

intro:
Bu mavzuda will ning yana bir muhim ishlatilishini o'rganamiz: gapirayotgan paytda qilingan qaror va yordam taklifi.

The phone is ringing. — I'll answer it! (Telefon jiringlayapti. — Men ko'taraman!) — qaror hozir qilindi.

Taklif uchun Shall I…? / Shall we…?: Shall I help you? (Yordam beraymi?)
explain:
1. Hozir qilingan qaror: I'll

Oldindan reja yo'q, shu daqiqada qaror qilinadi:
• I'm cold. — I'll close the window. (Sovqotyapman. — Derazani yopaman.)
• I'm hungry. — I'll make you a sandwich. (Ochman. — Senga buterbrod qilib beraman.)
• Which one? — I'll take the blue one. (Qaysi biri? — Ko'kini olaman.)

2. Va'da va rad etish

• I'll call you tomorrow. I promise. (Ertaga qo'ng'iroq qilaman. Va'da beraman.)
• The door won't open. (Eshik ochilmayapti.)

3. Shall I / Shall we

ShaklMa'nosiMisol
Shall I…?…aymi? (yordam taklifi)Shall I open the door?
Shall we…?…aylikmi? (taklif)Shall we go out?
What shall we…?Nima qilaylik?What shall we eat?

4. Reja bo'lsa — will emas

• I'm going to visit Ali tomorrow. (oldindan reja)
• Oh, Ali is ill? I'll visit him. (hozir qaror)
tip: O'zbekchadagi "-aymi?" (ochaymi? yordam beraymi?) = Shall I…?; "-aylikmi?" (boraylikmi?) = Shall we…?
ex: It's dark. I'll turn on the light.
What shall we do this weekend?

title: might
lesson:
might + verb = balki, ehtimol (aniq emas)

• I might go to the party.
(Balki ziyofatga borarman.)
• It might rain later.
(Keyinroq yomg'ir yog'ishi mumkin.)
• She might not come.
(U kelmasligi mumkin.)

⚠️ might dan keyin fe'l asosiy shaklda: might go (not goes / to go)

q.q: I ___ go to the party. I'm not sure.
She ___ not come. She's very busy.
I might ___ to London next year. (go)
Where are you going on holiday? — I'm not sure. I ___ go to Turkey.
q.uz: Ta'tilga qayerga borasiz? — Bilmayman. Balki Turkiyaga borarman.
Ehtiyot bo'ling. O'zingizga shikast yetkazishingiz mumkin.

q.q: He ___ not be at home. Call him first.
q.uz: U uyda bo'lmasligi mumkin. Avval qo'ng'iroq qiling.

intro:
Might — "balki, ehtimol" degan ma'noni beradi. Biz uni aniq bo'lmagan, bo'lishi ham, bo'lmasligi ham mumkin bo'lgan narsalar uchun ishlatamiz.

I might go to the party. (Balki ziyofatga borarman — hali aniq emas.)
It might rain. (Yomg'ir yog'ishi mumkin.)
explain:
1. Shakli

might + fe'l (1-shakl) — barcha shaxslar uchun bir xil.
Misol
+She might come.
−She might not come.

2. will va might farqi

GapIshonch
I will go.100% — aniq boraman
I'll probably go.~80% — ehtimol boraman
I might go.~50% — balki borarman
I might not go.~50% — bormasligim ham mumkin

3. Qachon ishlatiladi?

• Rejalar aniq bo'lmaganda: We might go to Turkey this summer. (Bu yoz balki Turkiyaga borarmiz.)
• Ogohlantirish: Be careful, you might fall. (Ehtiyot bo'ling, yiqilishingiz mumkin.)

4. Eslab qoling

might dan keyin to yo'q va fe'lga -s qo'shilmaydi: She might be late (not might is, might to be).
tip: O'zbekchadagi "balki …-ar" (balki borarman) yoki "…-ishi mumkin" (yog'ishi mumkin) might ga to'g'ri keladi.
ex: Take an umbrella. It might rain.
She might not know the answer.
We might buy a new car next year.
Keyingi yil balki yangi mashina olarmiz.
Don't touch it. It might be hot.
U keyinroq sizga qo'ng'iroq qilishi mumkin.

title: can and could
lesson:
can — qila olaman (hozir) · could — qila olardim (o'tmishda)

• I can swim.
(Men suza olaman.)
• She can't drive.
(U mashina hayday olmaydi.)
• When I was young, I could run fast.
(Yoshligimda tez yugura olardim.)

Iltimos: Can / Could you help me?
(Menga yordam bera olasizmi?)

q.q: I ___ swim, but I can't dive.
q.uz: Men suza olaman, lekin sho'ng'iy olmayman.
U mashina hayday olmaydi. Hech o'rganmagan.

q.q: When I was young, I ___ run very fast.
I was tired, but I ___ sleep. (negative, past)
I'm sorry, I ___ come to your party yesterday.

intro:
Can — qila olmoq (qobiliyat, imkoniyat). Could — uning o'tgan zamoni: qila olardim.

I can swim. (Men suza olaman.)
When I was five, I could read. (Besh yoshimda o'qiy olardim.)

Ularni iltimos va ruxsat so'rash uchun ham ishlatamiz: Can I come in? Could you help me?
explain:
1. Shakli

can / could + fe'l (1-shakl) — barcha shaxslar uchun bir xil.
HozirO'tgan
+I can drive.I could drive.
−I can't (cannot) drive.I couldn't drive.
?Can you drive?Could you drive?

2. Qachon ishlatiladi?

• Qobiliyat: She can speak three languages. (U uch tilda gapira oladi.)
• O'tmishdagi qobiliyat: I couldn't sleep last night. (Kecha uxlay olmadim.)
• Ruxsat so'rash: Can / Could I use your phone? (Telefoningizdan foydalansam bo'ladimi?)
• Iltimos: Could you open the window, please? (Derazani ochib bera olasizmi?)
Could — can ga qaraganda muloyimroq.

3. Eslab qoling

• can dan keyin to yo'q: I can swim (not can to swim).
• -s qo'shilmaydi: She can drive (not cans, can drives).
tip: O'zbekchadagi "-a olaman" (suza olaman) = can; "-a olardim / -a olmadim" = could / couldn't; "…sam bo'ladimi?" = Can I…?
ex: She could read when she was four.
We couldn't go out because of the rain.
Could you speak more slowly, please?

title: must / mustn't / don't need to
lesson:
must — shart, zarur: I must go now.
(Hozir ketishim shart.)
mustn't — mumkin emas, taqiqlangan: You mustn't smoke here.
(Bu yerda chekish mumkin emas.)
don't need to — shart emas: You don't need to come.
(Kelishingiz shart emas.)

O'tmishda: must → had to: I had to work yesterday.
(Kecha ishlashga majbur bo'ldim.)

q.q: You ___ bring food. There's a lot here.
q.uz: Ovqat olib kelishingiz shart emas. Bu yerda ko'p.
q.w: Ovqat ko'p, olib kelish shart emas → don't need to.
must ning o'tgan zamoni → had to.

q.q: You ___ tell anybody. It's a secret.
q.uz: Hech kimga aytmasligingiz kerak. Bu sir.

q.q: We ___ hurry. We have lots of time.
q.w: Vaqt ko'p, shoshilish shart emas → don't need to.

q.q: You ___ wear a seat belt in the car.

intro:
Bu mavzuda majburiyat va taqiq haqida gapirishni o'rganamiz:
• must — shart, albatta kerak: You must wear a seat belt. (Xavfsizlik kamarini taqishingiz shart.)
• mustn't — mumkin emas, taqiqlangan: You mustn't smoke here. (Bu yerda chekish mumkin emas.)
• don't need to — shart emas: You don't need to come. (Kelishingiz shart emas.)
explain:
1. Shakli

must / mustn't + fe'l (1-shakl) · don't need to + fe'l

2. Uchalasini solishtiring

So'zMa'nosiMisol
mustshart, zarurI must go now.
mustn'tqilish mumkin emasYou mustn't be late.
don't need toqilish shart emas, xohlasang qilYou don't need to pay.

3. mustn't va don't need to — eng ko'p adashtiriladi

• You mustn't tell him. — aytish taqiqlangan (sir).
• You don't need to tell him. — aytish shart emas (u allaqachon biladi).

4. O'tgan zamon

must ning o'tgan zamon shakli yo'q, o'rniga had to ishlatiladi:
• I had to work late yesterday. (Kecha kechgacha ishlashga majbur bo'ldim.)
• We didn't need to wait. (Kutishimiz shart bo'lmadi.)
tip: O'zbekchada: must = "…ishim shart / kerak", mustn't = "…ish mumkin emas", don't need to = "…ish shart emas". "Mumkin emas" va "shart emas" ni adashtirmang!
ex: I must call my mother today.
You mustn't use your phone in the exam.
You don't need to bring anything.
Hech narsa olib kelishingiz shart emas.
I had to get up at 5 this morning.
Bugun ertalab soat 5 da turishga majbur bo'ldim.
mi: You don't need to pay. It's free.

title: should
lesson:
should + verb — maslahat: ... qilish kerak, yaxshi bo'ladi

• You should go to bed early.
(Erta yotishingiz kerak.)
• You shouldn't eat so much sugar.
(Shuncha ko'p shakar yemasligingiz kerak.)
• I think you should see a doctor.
(Menimcha, shifokorga ko'rinishingiz kerak.)
• Should I call him?
(Unga qo'ng'iroq qilsammikan?)

q.q: You look tired. You ___ go to bed.
I think you should ___ a doctor.
___ I call him or send a message?
q.uz: Unga qo'ng'iroq qilaymi yoki xabar yuboraymi?

q.q: It's a great film. You ___ watch it.
q.uz: Ajoyib film. Uni albatta ko'rishingiz kerak.

q.q: He ___ drive so fast. It's dangerous. (negative)
q.uz: U bunchalik tez haydamasligi kerak. Xavfli.

intro:
Should — maslahat berish uchun ishlatiladi: "…ish kerak", "…sang yaxshi bo'ladi". Bu buyruq emas, faqat yaxshi fikr.

You look tired. You should go to bed. (Charchagan ko'rinasiz. Yotishingiz kerak.)
You shouldn't eat so much sugar. (Shuncha ko'p shakar yemasligingiz kerak.)
explain:
1. Shakli

should + fe'l (1-shakl) — barcha shaxslar uchun bir xil.
Misol
+You should see a doctor.
−You shouldn't drive so fast.
?Should I call him?

2. Qachon ishlatiladi?

• Maslahat berish: You should read this book. It's great. (Bu kitobni o'qishingiz kerak. Ajoyib.)
• Fikr bildirish: I think the government should build more schools. (Menimcha, hukumat ko'proq maktab qurishi kerak.)
• Maslahat so'rash: What should I do? (Nima qilishim kerak?)

3. should va must farqi

• You must stop at a red light. — qoida, majburiy.
• You should drink more water. — maslahat, yaxshi bo'ladi.

Ko'pincha I think / I don't think bilan keladi:
I don't think you should go. (Menimcha, bormaganingiz ma'qul.)
tip: O'zbekchadagi "…ish kerak" (maslahat ma'nosida) va "…sang yaxshi bo'ladi" = should. "…masang yaxshi" = shouldn't.
ex: Children shouldn't watch too much TV.

title: I have to ...
lesson:
have to / has to = majburman (qoida, vaziyat sababli)

• I have to work on Saturdays.
(Shanba kunlari ishlashim kerak.)
• She has to wear a uniform.
(U forma kiyishi shart.)
• I had to wait for an hour.
(Bir soat kutishga majbur bo'ldim.)

don't have to = shart emas: You don't have to pay.
(To'lashingiz shart emas.)
Question: Do you have to …?

q.q: She ___ wear a uniform at work.
I ___ wait for an hour yesterday. (have to — past)
q.uz: Kecha bir soat kutishga majbur bo'ldim.

q.w: Bepul — to'lash shart emas → don't have to.

q.q: He ___ get up early tomorrow. It's Sunday.
q.uz: U ertaga erta turishi shart emas. Yakshanba.
q.w: Yakshanba — erta turish shart emas; he → doesn't have to.

q.q: What time ___ you have to leave yesterday?
q.uz: Kecha soat nechada ketishingiz kerak edi?

intro:
Have to — "majburman, …ishim kerak". Biz uni qoida yoki vaziyat sababli majburiy bo'lgan ishlar uchun ishlatamiz.

I have to work on Saturdays. (Shanba kunlari ishlashim kerak — ish qoidasi shunaqa.)
don't have to = shart emas: You don't have to pay. (To'lashingiz shart emas.)
explain:
1. Shakli

HozirO'tgan
+I/you/we/they have to
he/she/it has to		had to
−don't / doesn't have todidn't have to
?Do / Does … have to?Did … have to?

2. Misollar

• She has to wear a uniform at work. (U ishda forma kiyishi shart.)
• I had to wait for two hours. (Ikki soat kutishga majbur bo'ldim.)
• Do you have to go now? (Hozir ketishingiz kerakmi?)
• He doesn't have to get up early. (Unga erta turish shart emas.)

3. must va have to

Ma'nosi deyarli bir xil, lekin:
• must — gapiruvchining o'z fikri: I must study more. (o'zim shunday deb hisoblayman)
• have to — tashqi qoida/vaziyat: I have to study — tomorrow is the exam.
O'tgan zamonda faqat had to.

4. Diqqat!

mustn't = mumkin emas, don't have to = shart emas. Ma'nosi butunlay boshqa!
tip: O'zbekchadagi "…ishim kerak / majburman" = have to; "…ish shart emas" = don't have to; "…ishga majbur bo'ldim" = had to.
ex: I have to go to the bank today.
My sister has to take her medicine every day.
Opam har kuni dori ichishi kerak.
We had to walk because there were no buses.
Avtobus yo'qligi uchun piyoda yurishga majbur bo'ldik.
You don't have to come if you're busy.
Does he have to work tomorrow?
Did you have to pay for parking?
To'xtash joyi uchun to'lashingizga to'g'ri keldimi?

title: Would you like ...? I'd like ...
lesson:
Would you like …? — taklif (Xohlaysizmi?)
I'd like … (I would like) — xohlayman (muloyim)

• Would you like some tea?
(Choy ichasizmi?)
• Would you like to go out tonight?
(Bugun kechqurun tashqariga chiqishni xohlaysizmi?)
• I'd like a cup of coffee, please.
(Bir piyola qahva bering, iltimos.)

⚠️ Do you like tea? = umuman yoqtirasizmi? · Would you like tea? = hozir xohlaysizmi?

q.q: I'd ___ a cup of coffee, please.
Would you like ___ to the cinema tonight?
I ___ like to visit Japan one day.
Would you like some cake? — No, thank you. I'm ___ hungry.
q.uz: Tort yeysizmi? — Yo'q, rahmat. Och emasman.
q.w: No, thank you. I'm not hungry.

q.q: I'd like ___ speak to the manager, please.

intro:
Bu mavzuda muloyim taklif va istak bildirishni o'rganamiz:
• Would you like…? — …xohlaysizmi? (taklif): Would you like some tea? (Choy ichasizmi?)
• I'd like… — …xohlardim (muloyim so'rash): I'd like a coffee, please. (Menga qahva bering, iltimos.)

Bu "I want" ga qaraganda ancha muloyim eshitiladi.
explain:
1. Shakli

+ narsa+ fe'l
TaklifWould you like some tea?Would you like to come?
IstakI'd like a sandwich.I'd like to go home.
I'd = I would. Fe'ldan oldin doim to keladi.

2. Do you like va Would you like farqi

Do you like…?Would you like…?
Umuman yoqtirasizmi?Hozir xohlaysizmi?
Do you like tea? — Yes, I love it.Would you like tea? — Yes, please.

3. Javob berish

Would you like some cake?
• Yes, please. (Ha, rahmat.)
• No, thank you. (Yo'q, rahmat.)
"Yes, I would like" deyish shart emas.

4. Restoran va do'konda

• I'd like a table for two, please.
• What would you like to drink? (Nima ichasiz?)
tip: O'zbekchada mehmonga "Choy ichasizmi?" deymiz. Inglizchada buning eng muloyim shakli — Would you like some tea? "Do you want tea?" qo'polroq eshitiladi.
ex: Would you like a cup of coffee?
I'd like to book a room, please.
Would you like to come to my party?
What would you like for lunch?
I'd like some information about the course.
Would you like to sit down? — Yes, please.
mi: Do you like a coffee now?
Would you like a coffee now?
Would you like coffee? — Yes, I like.
Would you like coffee? — Yes, please.

title: Do this! Don't do that! Let's do this!
lesson:
Buyruq: fe'lning asosiy shakli
• Come here!
(Bu yerga keling!)
• Please sit down.
(Iltimos, o'tiring.)

Inkor: Don't + verb
• Don't be late!
(Kechikmang!)

Taklif: Let's (let us) + verb
• Let's go to the park.
(Bog'ga boraylik.)
• Let's not go out.
(Tashqariga chiqmaylik.)

q.q: ___ be late! The lesson starts at 9.
It's a nice day. ___ go to the park.
I'm tired. — ___ have a rest then.

intro:
Bu mavzuda buyruq gaplar va taklif qilishni o'rganamiz:
• Buyruq: fe'lning asosiy shakli bilan boshlanadi: Come here! (Bu yerga keling!)
• Inkor buyruq: Don't + fe'l: Don't be late! (Kechikmang!)
• Birga qilishni taklif: Let's + fe'l: Let's go! (Ketdik! / Boraylik!)
explain:
1. Buyruq gap (imperative)

Ega (you) aytilmaydi, gap fe'l bilan boshlanadi:
• Open the window, please. (Derazani oching, iltimos.)
• Sit down. (O'tiring.)
• Be careful! (Ehtiyot bo'ling!)
please qo'shilsa muloyimroq bo'ladi.

2. Inkor buyruq

Don't + fe'l:
• Don't touch it! (Tegmang!)
• Don't worry. (Xavotir olmang.)

3. Let's — taklif

ShaklMisolMa'nosi
Let's + fe'lLet's eat.Ovqatlanaylik.
Let's not + fe'lLet's not go out.Tashqariga chiqmaylik.
Let's = let us. Fe'l 1-shaklda, to siz: Let's go (not Let's to go).
tip: O'zbekchadagi buyruq ("kel", "keling") inglizchada fe'lning asosiy shakli bo'ladi: Come. "-aylik" qo'shimchasi (boraylik, o'ynaylik) = Let's.
ex: Be quiet, please. The baby is sleeping.

title: I used to ...
lesson:
used to + verb — o'tmishda odat bo'lgan, endi yo'q

• I used to play football. (Now I don't.)
(Ilgari futbol o'ynardim. Hozir o'ynamayman.)
• She used to live in Bukhara.
(U ilgari Buxoroda yashardi.)

Negative: didn't use to · Question: Did you use to …?
• I didn't use to like tea.
(Ilgari choyni yoqtirmasdim.)

q.q: I ___ to play football, but now I don't.
I ___ use to like tea, but now I love it.
q.uz: Ilgari choyni yoqtirmasdim, hozir juda yoqtiraman.

q.q: ___ you use to play the piano?
This building ___ a cinema. Now it's a shop.
q.uz: Bu bino ilgari kinoteatr edi. Endi do'kon.

q.q: We used to ___ to the sea every summer. (go)
He ___ to smoke, but he stopped.

intro:
Used to — o'tmishdagi odat yoki holat, hozir esa bunday emas.

I used to play football. (Ilgari futbol o'ynardim — hozir o'ynamayman.)
She used to live in Bukhara. (U ilgari Buxoroda yashardi.)

O'zbek tilida bunga "ilgari …-ardim" to'g'ri keladi.
explain:
1. Shakli

ShaklMisol
+used to + fe'lI used to smoke.
−didn't use to + fe'lI didn't use to like fish.
?Did … use to + fe'l?Did you use to play?
⚠️ Inkor va savolda -d tushib qoladi: did … use to (did dan keyin 1-shakl).

2. Qachon ishlatiladi?

• O'tmishdagi odat: We used to go to the sea every summer. (Har yozda dengizga borardik.)
• O'tmishdagi holat: This shop used to be a cinema. (Bu do'kon ilgari kinoteatr edi.)
Ikkala holatda ham bu narsa hozir yo'q.

3. Hozirgi odat uchun ishlatilmaydi

Hozirgi odat uchun present simple: I usually go to the gym. (not I use to go)
tip: O'zbekchadagi "ilgari …-ardim / …-ardi" (ilgari chekardim, ilgari shu yerda yashardi) = used to.
ex: I used to have long hair.
My grandfather used to work in a factory.
We used to live near the river.
I didn't use to like vegetables.
Did you use to play with dolls?
There used to be a park here.
Ilgari bu yerda bog' bor edi.
mi: I used to go to the gym now.
I usually go to the gym now.

title: there is / there are
lesson:
Biror narsa bor ekanini aytish uchun:
there is (there's) + birlik · there are + ko'plik

• There's a bank near here.
(Bu yer yaqinida bank bor.)
• There are five people in my family.
(Oilamizda besh kishi bor.)
• There isn't a hotel here.
(Bu yerda mehmonxona yo'q.)
• Is there a supermarket near here?
(Bu yer yaqinida supermarket bormi?)

q.q: There ___ five people in my family.
There ___ a hotel in this village. (negative)
How many students ___ there in your class?
There ___ any eggs in the fridge.
Is there a park near your house? — Yes, there ___.

intro:
There is / there are — biror joyda biror narsa bor ekanini aytish uchun ishlatiladi.

There is a bank near here. (Bu yer yaqinida bank bor.)
There are five people in my family. (Oilamizda besh kishi bor.)

Diqqat: "Mening mashinam bor" (egalik) uchun emas, u I have bo'ladi (Unit 9). There is — joyda mavjudlik.
explain:
1. Shakli

BirlikKo'plik
+There is (there's) a…There are some…
−There isn't a…There aren't any…
?Is there a…?Are there any…?

2. Qachon ishlatiladi?

Biror joyda nimadir bor yoki yo'qligini aytganda:
• There's a problem. (Muammo bor.)
• There are a lot of shops in this street. (Bu ko'chada do'konlar ko'p.)
• Is there a pharmacy near here? (Bu yer yaqinida dorixona bormi?)
• How many students are there in your class? (Sinfingizda nechta o'quvchi bor?)

3. Sanalmaydigan otlar bilan

Sanalmaydigan otlar bilan there is ishlatiladi: There is some milk. There isn't any water.

4. Qisqa javoblar

Is there a hotel? — Yes, there is. / No, there isn't.
tip: O'zbekchada "Bu yerda bank bor" deymiz va "bor" so'zi oxirida keladi. Inglizchada esa There is gapning boshida turadi: There is a bank here.
ex: There's a café on the corner.
There are two bedrooms in our flat.
There isn't any bread. Can you buy some?
There's a lot of traffic today.
Is there a bus to the airport? — Yes, there is.
mi: Is there a hotel near here?
In my room is a bed.
There is a bed in my room.

title: there was / were — there has been — there will be
lesson:
• There was a party last night.
(Kecha kechqurun ziyofat bo'ldi.)
• There were many people at the concert.
(Konsertda odam ko'p edi.)
• There has been an accident.
(Avariya bo'libdi.)
• There will be a meeting tomorrow.
(Ertaga yig'ilish bo'ladi.)

q.q: There ___ many people at the concert.
There ___ be a meeting tomorrow at 10.
___ a lot of rain last week?
q.w: rain — sanalmaydi, o'tmish savol → Was there.

q.q: There ___ been a lot of changes in our city. (present perfect)

intro:
Bu mavzuda there is / there are ning boshqa zamonlardagi shakllarini o'rganamiz:
• there was / there were — bor edi (o'tmish): There was a party. (Ziyofat bo'ldi.)
• there has been / there have been — bo'libdi (natija hozir): There has been an accident.
• there will be — bo'ladi (kelajak): There will be a meeting tomorrow.
explain:
1. Zamonlar jadvali

ZamonBirlikKo'plik
Hozirthere isthere are
O'tganthere wasthere were
Present perfectthere has beenthere have been
Kelajakthere will be (ikkalasiga ham)

2. Misollar

• There was a good film on TV last night. (Kecha televizorda yaxshi film bor edi.)
• There were a lot of people at the wedding. (To'yda odam ko'p edi.)
• There has been a lot of rain this week. (Bu hafta yomg'ir ko'p yog'di.)
• There will be snow tomorrow. (Ertaga qor yog'adi.)

3. Inkor va savol

• There wasn't any water. · Were there any problems?
• There won't be any lessons on Monday. (Dushanba kuni dars bo'lmaydi.)
tip: O'zbekchadagi "bor edi" = there was/were, "bo'libdi / bo'ldi" (natija) = there has been, "bo'ladi" (kelajak) = there will be.
ex: There was a big storm last night.
There were no taxis at the station.
There has been an accident on the main road.
There will be a test next week.
mi: It was a party last night.
There was a party last night.

title: It ...
lesson:
Vaqt, ob-havo, masofa va baho uchun it ishlatiladi:

• It's 5 o'clock.
(Soat besh.)
• It's raining. · It's cold today.
(Yomg'ir yog'yapti. · Bugun sovuq.)
• It's 10 kilometres from here to the city.
(Bu yerdan shahargacha 10 km.)
• It's nice to see you.
(Sizni ko'rganimdan xursandman.)

⚠️ It is cold. (not Is cold.)

q.q: How far is ___ from here to the airport?

intro:
Ingliz tilida gapda ega bo'lishi shart. Shuning uchun vaqt, ob-havo, masofa va baholash haqida gapirganda, ega o'rniga it ishlatiladi. Bu "it" hech narsani bildirmaydi, shunchaki bo'sh ega.

It's 5 o'clock. (Soat besh.) · It's raining. (Yomg'ir yog'yapti.) · It's cold. (Sovuq.)
explain:
1. Qachon it ishlatiladi?

MavzuMisol
Vaqt, kun, sanaIt's half past six. It's Monday.
Ob-havoIt's sunny. It's snowing.
MasofaIt's 5 km to the city.
BaholashIt's nice to meet you. It's difficult to learn.

2. Eng ko'p xato

O'zbekchada "Sovuq", "Soat 5" deymiz va ega yo'q. Inglizchada "Is cold" deb bo'lmaydi, albatta It qo'yiladi: It is cold.

3. It va There farqi

• There is — nimadir bor: There's a hotel near here.
• It is — narsani tasvirlash: It's a big hotel.
• How far is it to the station? (Vokzalgacha qancha masofa?)
tip: O'zbekcha egasiz gaplar ("Issiq", "Kech bo'ldi", "Qiziq") inglizchada It bilan boshlanadi: It's hot. It's late. It's interesting.
ex: It's 7 o'clock. Time to get up!
It's 300 kilometres from Tashkent to Samarkand.
Is it easy to make plov? — No, it isn't!

title: I am, I don't, etc.
lesson:
Fe'lni takrorlamaslik uchun faqat yordamchi fe'l ishlatamiz:

• She isn't tired, but I am.
(U charchamagan, lekin men charchadim.)
• I don't like fish, but my sister does.
(Men baliqni yoqtirmayman, opam esa yoqtiradi.)
• He can swim, but I can't.
(U suza oladi, lekin men suza olmayman.)
• Are you hungry? — Yes, I am.

q.q: I don't like fish, but my sister ___.
q.uz: Men baliqni yoqtirmayman, opam esa yoqtiradi.
q.w: don't like (oddiy fe'l) → but my sister does.

q.uz: U suza oladi, lekin men suza olmayman.

q.q: I wasn't at home, but my parents ___.
q.uz: Men uyda emas edim, ota-onam esa uyda edi.

q.q: Tom has a car, but I ___.
I've seen the film, but my friend ___.
q.uz: Men filmni ko'rganman, do'stim esa ko'rmagan.

q.q: Did you go to the party? — No, I ___.

intro:
Ingliz tilida fe'lni takrorlamaslik uchun faqat yordamchi fe'l (am, is, do, does, did, have, can, will…) ishlatiladi.

She isn't tired, but I am. (U charchamagan, men esa charchadim.)
I don't like fish, but my sister does. (Men baliqni yoqtirmayman, opam esa yoqtiradi.)
explain:
1. Qaysi yordamchi fe'l?

Birinchi gapdagi fe'lga qarang:
Birinchi gapQisqa javob/qism
am / is / are… but I am / he isn't
oddiy fe'l (hozir)… but she does / I don't
oddiy fe'l (o'tgan)… but I did / they didn't
have done… but I have / he hasn't
can / will… but I can't / she won't

2. Misollar

• He can swim, but I can't. (U suza oladi, men esa suza olmayman.)
• I wasn't at home, but my parents were. (Men uyda emas edim, ota-onam esa uyda edi.)
• Do you like tea? — Yes, I do.
• Have you finished? — No, I haven't.

3. Qoida

Qisqa javobda asosiy fe'l takrorlanmaydi: "Yes, I do" (not Yes, I like).
tip: O'zbekchada "men ham", "u esa yo'q" deymiz. Inglizchada esa yordamchi fe'l kerak: but I am, but she doesn't. Bu juda tabiiy, ko'p ishlatiladigan shakl.
ex: I'm not hungry, but Ali is.
Men och emasman, Ali esa och.
She doesn't speak French, but her brother does.
U fransuzcha gapirmaydi, akasi esa gapiradi.
I didn't see the film, but my friends did.
Men filmni ko'rmadim, do'stlarim esa ko'rishdi.
We can't come, but they can.
Biz kela olmaymiz, ular esa kela oladi.
Are you tired? — Yes, I am.
Have you been to Bukhara? — No, I haven't.
mi: I don't like it, but she likes.
I don't like it, but she does.
Are you ready? — Yes, I am.
He can't swim, but I do.
He can't swim, but I can.
Did you go? — Yes, I went.
Did you go? — Yes, I did.

title: Have you? Are you? Don't you? etc.
lesson:
Qiziqish bildirish uchun qisqa savol:
• I'm tired. — Are you?
(Charchadim. — Shundaymi?)
• I don't like tea. — Don't you?
(Choyni yoqtirmayman. — Rostdanmi?)

Gap oxiridagi so'roq (tag): ijobiy gap → inkor tag, inkor gap → ijobiy tag
• It's cold, isn't it?
(Sovuq, shunday emasmi?)
• You aren't busy, are you?
(Band emassiz, to'g'rimi?)

q.q: I was ill last week. — ___ you? I didn't know.
q.uz: O'tgan hafta kasal edim. — Shundaymi? Bilmagan ekanman.

intro:
Bu mavzuda ikki narsani o'rganamiz:
1) Qisqa javob-savol — suhbatdoshga qiziqish bildirish uchun: I'm tired. — Are you? (Shundaymi?)
2) Gap oxiridagi so'roq (question tag) — fikrimizni tasdiqlatish uchun: It's cold, isn't it? (Sovuq, shunday emasmi?)
explain:
1. Javob-savol (Are you? Do you?)

Suhbatdosh gapidagi yordamchi fe'lni olib, savol qilamiz:
• I'm hungry. — Are you?
• I don't like coffee. — Don't you?
• I was in London. — Were you?
• She has two sisters. — Has she? / Does she?
Bu o'zbekchadagi "Shundaymi? Rostdanmi?" ga to'g'ri keladi.

2. Question tag

GapTagMisol
Ijobiy (+)inkor (−)It's nice, isn't it?
Inkor (−)ijobiy (+)You aren't busy, are you?
Tag'da gapdagi yordamchi fe'l va ega olmoshi ishlatiladi:
• Ali lives here, doesn't he? (lives → does)
• You've seen it, haven't you?
• They can't swim, can they?
• She went home, didn't she?
tip: O'zbekchadagi "…, shunday emasmi? / …, to'g'rimi?" = question tag. Inglizchada u gapdagi fe'lga qarab o'zgaradi: isn't it, don't you, didn't she.
ex: I've just bought a car. — Have you? What kind?
Hozirgina mashina sotib oldim. — Shundaymi? Qanaqasini?
It's a beautiful day, isn't it?
They went to Bukhara, didn't they?

title: too / either — so am I / neither do I
lesson:
Ijobiy gapga qo'shilish: too yoki So + aux + I
• I'm hungry. — I am too. / So am I.
(Men ham.)
• I like tea. — So do I.

Inkor gapga qo'shilish: either yoki Neither + aux + I
• I can't swim. — I can't either. / Neither can I.
(Men ham suza olmayman.)

q.w: I like (present simple) → So do I.

q.q: I didn't see the film. — Neither ___ I.
q.w: I didn't see → Neither did I.

q.q: I've been to Istanbul. — So ___ I.
I wasn't at home. — Neither ___ I.

intro:
Bu mavzuda "men ham" va "men ham … emas" deyishni o'rganamiz.

• Ijobiy gapga qo'shilish: I'm tired. — So am I. / I am too. (Men ham.)
• Inkor gapga qo'shilish: I can't swim. — Neither can I. / I can't either. (Men ham suza olmayman.)

1. Ijobiy gapga: too / So + yordamchi + I

GaptooSo…
I'm hungry.I am too.So am I.
I like tea.I do too.So do I.
I went home.I did too.So did I.
I can swim.I can too.So can I.

2. Inkor gapga: either / Neither + yordamchi + I

GapeitherNeither…
I'm not tired.I'm not either.Neither am I.
I don't smoke.I don't either.Neither do I.
I didn't go.I didn't either.Neither did I.

3. Eslab qoling

• So / Neither dan keyin so'z tartibi teskari: So am I (not So I am).
• Yordamchi fe'l birinchi gapdagiga mos: like → do, liked → did, have been → have.
• too — ijobiy, either — inkor.
tip: O'zbekchada ikkala holatda ham "men ham" deymiz. Inglizchada esa ijobiy gapga So do I / too, inkor gapga Neither do I / either ishlatiladi.
ex: I love Uzbek food. — So do I!
O'zbek taomlarini yaxshi ko'raman. — Men ham!
I'm from Tashkent. — So am I.
I didn't sleep well. — Neither did I.
I can't cook. — I can't either.
I've been to Khiva. — So have I.
I'm not ready. — Neither am I.
mi: I like tea. — So I do.
I like tea. — So do I.
I don't smoke. — I don't too.
I don't smoke. — I don't either.
I can't swim. — Neither can't I.
I can't swim. — Neither can I.
I went home. — So went I.
I went home. — So did I.

title: isn't / haven't / don't etc. (negatives)
lesson:
be: I'm not · isn't · aren't · wasn't · weren't
have (perfect): haven't · hasn't
will / can: won't · can't
simple: don't · doesn't · didn't + verb

• She isn't here.
(U bu yerda emas.)
• I haven't finished.
(Tugatmadim.)
• He didn't call me.
(U menga qo'ng'iroq qilmadi.)

q.q: Make negative: She is here. → She ___ here.
q.uz: Inkor qiling: U bu yerda emas.

q.q: Make negative: I have finished. → I ___ finished.
Make negative: He called me. → He ___ me.
q.uz: Inkor qiling: U menga qo'ng'iroq qilmadi.

q.q: Make negative: They will come. → They ___ come.
Make negative: She likes coffee. → She ___ coffee.
Make negative: We can swim. → We ___ swim.
Make negative: It was cold. → It ___ cold.

intro:
Bu mavzu — inkor gaplarni takrorlash. Ingliz tilida inkor not so'zi bilan yasaladi va u yordamchi fe'ldan keyin keladi. Qaysi yordamchi fe'l kerakligi zamonga bog'liq.

She is here → She isn't here.
I like it → I don't like it.
explain:
1. Inkor shakllari jadvali

I amI'm not
he is / they areisn't / aren't
was / werewasn't / weren't

I workedI didn't work

2. Qoida

• Gapda be, have, will, can bo'lsa → shunga not qo'shamiz.
• Gapda faqat oddiy fe'l bo'lsa → don't / doesn't / didn't + fe'lning 1-shakli.
• She works → she doesn't work (-s yo'qoladi).
• He went → he didn't go (2-shakl 1-shaklga qaytadi).

3. Bitta inkor yetarli

"I don't have no money" ❌ → I don't have any money ✅ yoki I have no money ✅
tip: O'zbekchada inkor fe'l ichida bo'ladi (bormadim). Inglizchada esa doim alohida so'z: not / don't / didn't. Avval gapda qaysi yordamchi fe'l borligini toping.

title: is it ...? have you ...? do they ...? (questions 1)
lesson:
Savolda yordamchi fe'l egadan oldin keladi:
you are → are you? · she has been → has she been?
you live → do you live? · he went → did he go?

• Where do you live?
(Qayerda yashaysiz?)
• What time did she arrive?
(U soat nechada keldi?)
• Have you seen my phone?
(Telefonimni ko'rdingizmi?)

q.uz: Bu yerda qancha vaqtdan beri turibsiz?

intro:
Bu mavzu — savol yasashni takrorlash. Ingliz tilida savolda yordamchi fe'l egadan oldinga chiqadi. Gapda yordamchi fe'l bo'lmasa, do / does / did qo'shiladi.

You are tired → Are you tired?
You live here → Do you live here?

1. Savol tartibi

(Savol so'zi) + yordamchi fe'l + ega + asosiy fe'l?
Darak gapSavol
She is working.What is she doing?
They have gone.Where have they gone?
He can swim.Can he swim?

They arrived.When did they arrive?

2. Qoida

• do/does/did dan keyin fe'l 1-shaklda: Where does she work? (not works)
• When did you arrive? (not arrived)

3. O'zbek tili bilan farq

O'zbekchada so'z tartibi o'zgarmaydi, faqat "-mi" qo'shiladi yoki savol so'zi qo'yiladi: "Siz qayerda yashaysiz?". Inglizchada esa tartib albatta o'zgaradi.
tip: O'zbekchada "Qayerda yashaysiz?" — savol so'zi + fe'l. Inglizchada: savol so'zi + do + you + live? "Where you live?" deb aytish eng ko'p uchraydigan xato.
ex: What time did the film start?
How long have you been here?
Bu yerda qancha vaqtdan beri turibsiz?
How often does he call you?
U sizga qanchalik tez-tez qo'ng'iroq qiladi?

title: Who saw you? Who did you see? (questions 2)
lesson:
Who/What ega bo'lsa — do/did ishlatilmaydi:
• Who saw you? (Somebody saw you.)
(Sizni kim ko'rdi?)
• What happened?
(Nima bo'ldi?)

Who/What to'ldiruvchi bo'lsa — do/did kerak:
• Who did you see? (You saw somebody.)
(Siz kimni ko'rdingiz?)

q.w: Javobda Ali — ega → Who saw you?
Javobda Ali — to'ldiruvchi (-ni) → Who did you see?

q.q: Who ___ the window? — Tom broke it.
What ___ you want? — I want a coffee.
Who ___ this book? — Navoi wrote it.
q.uz: Bu kitobni kim yozgan? — Navoiy yozgan.

q.q: Who ___ you call last night? — I called my mother.
q.uz: Kecha kechqurun kimga qo'ng'iroq qildingiz? — Onamga.

intro:
Bu mavzuda Who va What bilan ikki xil savolni farqlaymiz:

• Who saw you? — Sizni kim ko'rdi? (who — ega) → do/did kerak emas.
• Who did you see? — Siz kimni ko'rdingiz? (who — to'ldiruvchi) → do/did kerak.
explain:
1. Who / What — ega bo'lsa

Javobda ega o'rnida turgan narsa so'raladi. Gap tartibi darak gapdagidek, do/did yo'q:
• Somebody called. → Who called? (Kim qo'ng'iroq qildi?)
• Something happened. → What happened? (Nima bo'ldi?)
• Who lives in this house? (Bu uyda kim yashaydi?)

2. Who / What — to'ldiruvchi bo'lsa

Javobda to'ldiruvchi so'raladi, shuning uchun do/does/did kerak:
• You saw somebody. → Who did you see? (Kimni ko'rdingiz?)
• She wants something. → What does she want? (U nima xohlaydi?)

3. Solishtiring

SavolJavob

Who does Ali love?Ali loves Lola.
tip: O'zbekcha qo'shimchaga qarang: "Kim ko'rdi?" (ega) → Who saw? "Kimni ko'rdingiz?" (-ni, to'ldiruvchi) → Who did you see?
ex: Who did you meet at the party?
Who does this phone belong to?

title: Who is she talking to? What is it like?
lesson:
Predlog odatda savol oxirida qoladi:
• Who is she talking to?
(U kim bilan gaplashyapti?)
• Where are you from?
(Qayerdansiz?)
• What are you looking at?
(Nimaga qarayapsiz?)

What is it like? = U qanaqa? (tavsif so'raladi)
• What's your new teacher like? — She's very nice.
(Yangi o'qituvchingiz qanaqa? — Juda yoqimli.)

q.q: What's the weather ___ today? — It's sunny.
What's your new flat ___ ? — It's small but nice.
q.uz: Yangi kvartirangiz qanaqa? — Kichik, lekin yaxshi.

q.q: What is this book ___? — It's about history.
q.uz: Bu kitob nima haqida? — Tarix haqida.

q.q: Who did you go to the cinema ___?

intro:
Bu mavzuda predlogli savollarni o'rganamiz. Ingliz tilida predlog (to, from, at, for, with, about) ko'pincha savolning oxirida qoladi.

Who are you talking to? (Kim bilan gaplashyapsiz?)
Where are you from? (Qayerdansiz?)

Shuningdek, What is it like? — "U qanaqa?" degan savolni o'rganamiz.

1. Predlog oxirida

Darak gapSavol

I'm waiting for the bus.What are you waiting for?
The book is about war.What is the book about?
I went with Lola.Who did you go with?

2. What is … like?

like bu yerda "yoqtirmoq" emas, "o'xshash, qanaqa" degani. Biror narsa yoki odamni tasvirlab berishni so'raymiz:
• What's the weather like? — It's sunny. (Havo qanaqa? — Quyoshli.)
• What's your teacher like? — She's very kind. (O'qituvchingiz qanaqa? — Juda mehribon.)
• What was the film like? — Boring. (Film qanaqa edi? — Zerikarli.)
⚠️ "How is the weather like?" — xato. To'g'risi: What is the weather like?
tip: O'zbekchada predlog o'rniga qo'shimcha bor: "Kim bilan?", "Qayerdan?" — so'z boshida turadi. Inglizchada esa predlog savolning oxiriga o'tadi: Who … with? Where … from?
ex: Where does your friend come from?
Who did you go to the cinema with?
What was the weather like in Samarkand?

title: What ...? Which ...? How ...?
lesson:
What — umumiy, tanlov chegaralanmagan:
• What colour is your car?
(Mashinangiz qanday rangda?)
Which — kam variantdan tanlash:
• Which is your bag, this one or that one?
(Qaysi biri sizning sumkangiz, bumi yoki u?)
How + sifat: how old, how tall, how far, how often, how much, how many
• How far is it to the airport?
(Aeroportgacha qancha masofa?)

q.q: There are two bags. ___ one is yours?
q.uz: Ikkita sumka bor. Qaysi biri sizniki?

q.q: How ___ is it from here to the city centre? — 5 km.
q.uz: Bu yerdan shahar markazigacha qancha? — 5 km.

q.q: How ___ do you go to the gym? — Three times a week.
q.uz: Sport zaliga qanchalik tez-tez borasiz? — Haftada uch marta.

q.q: How ___ people were at the party? — About 50.
q.uz: Ziyofatda qancha odam bor edi? — 50 ga yaqin.

intro:
Bu mavzuda uchta savol so'zini farqlaymiz:
• What — nima? qanday? — tanlov chegaralanmagan: What colour is it?
• Which — qaysi? — bir nechta variantdan tanlash: Which bag is yours, this or that?
• How + sifat — qancha? qanchalik?: How old, how far, how much…

Which one do you want, the red or the blue?

How many children do they have?

title: How long does it take ...?
lesson:
Biror ishga qancha vaqt ketishini so'rash:
How long does it take (to do something)?

• How long does it take to get to the airport?
(Aeroportga yetib borish qancha vaqt oladi?)
• It takes 30 minutes by taxi.
(Taksida 30 daqiqa ketadi.)
• It took me two hours to do my homework.
(Uy vazifamni qilishga ikki soat ketdi.)

q.q: How long does it ___ to get to the airport?
It ___ me two hours to do my homework yesterday. (take)
q.uz: Kecha uy vazifamni qilishga ikki soat ketdi.

q.q: How long ___ it take you to get to work?
How long ___ it take to build the house? (past)
It takes an hour ___ there by car.
q.uz: U yerga mashinada borishga bir soat ketadi.

q.q: How ___ does it take to learn English?
q.uz: Ingliz tilini o'rganishga qancha vaqt ketadi?

q.q: It ___ three hours to fly to Istanbul.

intro:
Bu mavzuda biror ishga qancha vaqt ketishini so'rash va aytishni o'rganamiz.

How long does it take to get to the airport? (Aeroportga borish qancha vaqt oladi?)
It takes 30 minutes. (30 daqiqa ketadi.)

Bu yerda take — "vaqt olmoq, ketmoq" ma'nosida.

1. Shakli

Shakl

Javob (hozir)It takes (me) + vaqt + to + fe'l.
Javob (o'tgan)It took (me) + vaqt + to + fe'l.

2. Misollar

• It takes two hours to fly to Istanbul. (Istanbulga uchishga ikki soat ketadi.)
• It took me a week to read this book. (Bu kitobni o'qishga bir haftam ketdi.)
• How long did it take you to learn to drive? (Mashina haydashni o'rganishga qancha vaqtingiz ketdi?)

3. Eslab qoling

• Ega doim it: It takes… (not The road takes)
• Fe'ldan oldin to: to get, to do, to learn
• Kim uchun: It takes me / him / us…

ex: How long does it take to get to school?
It takes me 20 minutes to walk to work.
It took them three years to build the bridge.
Ko'prikni qurishga ularga uch yil ketdi.

title: Do you know where ...? I don't know what ...
lesson:
Ichki savolda so'z tartibi oddiy gapdagidek bo'ladi:
Where is the station? → Do you know where the station is?
What time does it start? → I don't know what time it starts.

• Do you know where Ali lives?
(Ali qayerda yashashini bilasizmi?)
• Ha/yo'q savollarda if: Do you know if she's at home?
(U uydami yoki yo'qmi, bilasizmi?)

q.w: Ichki savol: where + the station + is.

q.q: Do you know ___ she's at home? (yes/no question)
Can you tell me how much ___ ?
I wonder ___ he will come or not.

intro:
Bu mavzuda ichki savollarni o'rganamiz: "Vokzal qayerdaligini bilasizmi?", "U nima deganini bilmayman".

Ichki savolda so'z tartibi oddiy darak gapdagidek bo'ladi:
Where is the station? → Do you know where the station is?

1. Qoida

Do you know / Can you tell me / I don't know / I wonder + savol so'zi + ega + fe'l
Oddiy savolIchki savol

do / does / did ichki savolda yo'qoladi!

2. Ha/yo'q savollar → if / whether

• Is she at home? → Do you know if she is at home? (U uydami-yo'qmi, bilasizmi?)
• Did he call? → I don't know if he called.

3. Nima uchun kerak?

Ichki savol muloyimroq eshitiladi. Notanish odamdan nimadir so'raganda juda qulay:
Excuse me, could you tell me where the post office is?

ex: Do you know where Ali lives?
Can you tell me what time it is?
I don't know why she left.
Do you know if the shop is open?
I wonder how much this costs.
Could you tell me where the toilet is?

I don't know what time does it start.
I don't know what time it starts.
Do you know did he come?
Do you know if he came?

title: She said that ... He told me that ...
lesson:
Birovning so'zini yetkazganda zamon odatda bir pog'ona orqaga suriladi:
am/is → was · are → were · have → had · will → would · can → could · do → did

• "I'm tired." → She said (that) she was tired.
(U charchaganini aytdi.)
• "I'll call you." → He told me he would call me.
(U menga qo'ng'iroq qilishini aytdi.)

say something · tell somebody something

q.q: "I'll call you." → He said he ___ call me.
He ___ me that he was busy.
She ___ that she liked the film.
"I can swim." → Tom said he ___ swim.
"We are hungry." → They said they ___ hungry.
"I have lost my key." → She said she ___ lost her key.

intro:
Reported speech — o'zlashtirma gap, ya'ni birovning gapini boshqaga yetkazish: "U charchaganini aytdi".

Gapni yetkazganda zamon odatda bir pog'ona orqaga suriladi:
"I am tired." → She said (that) she was tired.
"I will call you." → He said he would call me.
explain:
1. Zamonlar qanday o'zgaradi

Ko'chirma gapO'zlashtirma gap
am / iswas
arewere
have / hashad
willwould
cancould
do / does (like)did (liked)

2. say va tell farqi

• say + (that) …: She said (that) she was busy. — kimga ekani aytilmaydi.
• tell + kishi + (that) …: She told me (that) she was busy. — kimga aytgani shart.
⚠️ "She said me" ❌ · "She told that" ❌

3. Olmoshlar ham o'zgaradi

"I love my job." → He said he loved his job.
that so'zini tushirib qoldirish mumkin.
tip: O'zbekchada: "U charchaganini aytdi" — fe'l o'zgaradi (charchaganini). Inglizchada ham zamon o'zgaradi: am → was. "Menga aytdi" = told me, oddiy "aytdi" = said.
ex: He told me he lived in Samarkand.
They said they would come later.
She told us she had lost her keys.
My mother said dinner was ready.
Onam kechki ovqat tayyor ekanini aytdi.
mi: She said me she was tired.
She told me she was tired.
He told that he was busy.
He said that he was busy.

title: work / working · go / going · do / doing
lesson:
Asosiy shakl (verb) — will, can, must, should, might, do/does/did dan keyin:
• I can swim. · Did you go?

to + verb — want, need, try, hope dan keyin:
• I want to go.

-ing — am/is/are/was/were dan keyin (continuous):
• She is working.

• He can't come.
(U kela olmaydi.)
• I need to buy some bread.
(Non sotib olishim kerak.)

q.q: They were ___ TV when I came. (watch)
q.uz: Men kelganimda ular televizor ko'rayotgan edi.
Sizni tez orada yana ko'rishga umid qilaman.

intro:
Ingliz tilida fe'l uch xil ko'rinishda keladi: work (asosiy shakl), to work, working. Qaysi biri kerakligi undan oldingi so'zga bog'liq.

• can / will / must / should / do + work
• want / need / hope + to work
• am / is / are / was + working
explain:
1. Asosiy shakl (to siz)

Quyidagi so'zlardan keyin:
will, can, could, must, should, might, would, do/does/did, let's
• I can swim. · Did you go? · You should rest.

2. to + fe'l

Quyidagi fe'llardan keyin:
want, need, hope, decide, try, learn, plan, would like, have to, be going to, used to
• I want to go. · She needs to study. · We're going to buy it.

3. -ing shakl

am / is / are / was / were dan keyin (davomli zamonlar):
• She is working. · They were sleeping.

4. Umumiy jadval

Oldingi so'zFe'l shakli
can, will, must, did…go
want, need, hope…to go
am, is, was…going
tip: O'zbekchada fe'l qo'shimchalar bilan o'zgaradi (bor-a olaman, bor-ish-ni xohlayman, bor-yap-man). Inglizchada esa fe'ldan oldingi so'zga qarab to'g'ri shaklni tanlaysiz.
ex: She is talking on the phone.

title: to ... (I want to do) and -ing (I enjoy doing)
lesson:
+ to: want, hope, decide, need, plan, learn, promise, forget
• I decided to leave.
(Ketishga qaror qildim.)

+ -ing: enjoy, finish, stop, mind, suggest, keep
• I enjoy reading.
(O'qishni yoqtiraman.)

Ikkalasi ham: like, love, hate, start, begin
• It started to rain / raining.

q.uz: Sizni tez orada ko'rishga umid qilaman.

q.q: Please stop ___ ! I'm trying to sleep.
q.uz: Iltimos, gapirishni bas qiling! Uxlashga harakat qilyapman.

q.q: She learnt ___ when she was five. (swim)

q.w: Inkor: not + to → not to be.

intro:
Ba'zi fe'llardan keyin ikkinchi fe'l to + fe'l shaklida, ba'zilaridan keyin esa -ing shaklida keladi. Buni har bir fe'l uchun yodlash kerak.

I decided to buy a car. (Mashina olishga qaror qildim.) — decide + to
I enjoy reading. (O'qishni yoqtiraman.) — enjoy + -ing
explain:
1. Fe'l + to

Fe'lMisol
want, need, hopeI hope to see you.
decide, plan, promiseHe promised to call.
learn, try, forgetShe learnt to drive.
agree, refuse, offerThey agreed to help.

2. Fe'l + -ing

Fe'lMisol
enjoy, mindDo you mind waiting?
finish, stopStop talking!
suggest, keepHe kept asking.
imagine, avoidAvoid eating late.

3. Ikkalasi ham mumkin

like, love, hate, start, begin, continue:
It started to rain. = It started raining.

4. Inkor

not to dan oldin: He promised not to be late. (U kechikmaslikka va'da berdi.)
tip: O'zbekchada ikkalasi ham ko'pincha "-ish" bilan tarjima qilinadi (o'qishni yoqtiraman, sotib olishga qaror qildim). Shuning uchun qaysi fe'ldan keyin to, qaysidan keyin -ing kelishini yodlash kerak.
ex: I enjoy cooking for my family.
U chet elda o'qishga qaror qildi.
Have you finished writing your essay?
Don't forget to lock the door.
Would you mind closing the window?
He promised not to tell anyone.
U hech kimga aytmaslikka va'da berdi.
mi: I hope to see you soon.

title: I want you to ... I told you to ...
lesson:
want / ask / tell / advise / would like + somebody + to + verb

• I want you to help me.
(Menga yordam berishingizni xohlayman.)
• She told me to wait.
(U menga kutishimni aytdi.)
• The doctor advised him to rest.
(Shifokor unga dam olishni maslahat berdi.)

⚠️ I want you to come. (not I want that you come)
make / let + somebody + verb (to siz): She let me go.

q.uz: Shifokor unga dam olishni maslahat berdi.

q.q: My parents won't let me ___ out late.
q.uz: Ota-onam kechgacha tashqarida yurishimga ruxsat bermaydi.

q.q: I asked Ali ___ close the door.
The teacher told us ___ to be late. (negative)

q.uz: U meni qayta qilishga majbur qildi.

intro:
Bu mavzuda boshqa odamdan biror narsa qilishini xohlash, so'rash, aytish haqida gapirishni o'rganamiz.

I want you to help me. (Menga yordam berishingizni xohlayman.)
She told me to wait. (U menga kutishimni aytdi.)

Tuzilishi: fe'l + kishi + to + fe'l.
explain:
1. Fe'l + kishi + to + fe'l

Fe'lMisolTarjima
wantI want you to come.Kelishingizni xohlayman.
would likeI'd like you to meet my wife.Rafiqam bilan tanishishingizni istardim.
askHe asked me to help.U mendan yordam so'radi.
tellShe told us to sit down.U bizga o'tirishni aytdi.
adviseThe doctor advised him to rest.Shifokor unga dam olishni maslahat berdi.
Kishi to'ldiruvchi shaklda: me, you, him, her, us, them.

2. Eng ko'p xato

O'zbekchadan to'g'ridan-to'g'ri tarjima qilib "I want that you help me" deyishadi. Bu xato!
✅ I want you to help me.

3. make va let — to siz!

• My mother made me clean my room. (Onam meni xonamni tozalashga majbur qildi.)
• My father let me drive his car. (Otam mashinasini haydashimga ruxsat berdi.)

4. Inkor

She told me not to worry. (U menga xavotir olmaslikni aytdi.)
tip: O'zbekcha "…ishingizni xohlayman" inglizchaga "that" bilan emas, want + you + to bilan tarjima qilinadi: I want you to come.
ex: I want you to be happy.
The teacher told us to open our books.
Can I ask you to help me?
My parents don't let me stay out late.
Ota-onam kechgacha tashqarida qolishimga ruxsat bermaydi.
She told me not to tell anyone.
U menga hech kimga aytmasligimni aytdi.
What do you want me to do?
mi: She told me to not worry.
She told me not to worry.

title: I went to the shop to ...
lesson:
Maqsadni aytish uchun to + verb:
• I went to the shop to buy bread.
(Non olish uchun do'konga bordim.)
• She called me to say hello.
(U salom berish uchun qo'ng'iroq qildi.)

for + noun:
• I went to the shop for some bread.
(Non uchun do'konga bordim.)

⚠️ I went there to buy … (not for buy / for to buy)

q.q: I went to the shop ___ some bread.
q.uz: Non sotib olish uchun do'konga bordim.

q.q: I went to the shop ___ some bread.

q.uz: U salom berish uchun qo'ng'iroq qildi.

q.q: We went to the café ___ a coffee.
I'm saving money ___ a new car.
q.uz: Yangi mashina olish uchun pul yig'yapman.

q.q: He went to London ___ study English.
q.uz: U ingliz tilini o'rganish uchun Londonga ketdi.

intro:
Bu mavzuda maqsadni aytishni o'rganamiz: nima uchun, nima maqsadda?

• to + fe'l: I went to the shop to buy bread. (Non sotib olish uchun do'konga bordim.)
• for + ot: I went to the shop for bread. (Non uchun do'konga bordim.)
explain:
1. to + fe'l — maqsad

• She called me to say hello. (U salom berish uchun qo'ng'iroq qildi.)
• I'm saving money to buy a car. (Mashina olish uchun pul yig'yapman.)
• We came here to see you. (Sizni ko'rgani keldik.)

2. for + ot

• Let's go out for a walk. (Sayr qilgani chiqaylik.)
• I went to the café for a coffee. (Qahva uchun kafega bordim.)
• This is a present for you. (Bu siz uchun sovg'a.)

3. Eng ko'p xato

❌ Xato✅ To'g'ri
I came here for see you.I came here to see you.
I went for to buy bread.I went to buy bread.
I went for buying bread.I went to buy bread.
Qoida: keyin fe'l kelsa → to, ot kelsa → for.
tip: O'zbekchadagi "…ish uchun / …gani" (olish uchun, ko'rgani) = to + fe'l. "…uchun" ot bilan (non uchun) = for + ot.
ex: I went to the bank to get some money.
She's learning English to get a better job.
U yaxshiroq ish topish uchun ingliz tilini o'rganyapti.
I called to ask about the price.
He went to the doctor for a check-up.
I need a knife to cut the bread.
mi: I went for to buy milk.
She studies for pass the exam.
She studies to pass the exam.

title: go to ... go on ... go for ... go -ing
lesson:
go to + joy: go to work, go to the bank
go on: go on holiday, go on a trip
go for: go for a walk, go for a swim, go for a drink
go + -ing (faoliyat): go shopping, go swimming, go skiing

• We went on holiday to Turkey.
(Ta'tilga Turkiyaga bordik.)
• Let's go for a walk.
(Sayr qilgani chiqaylik.)
• She goes shopping on Saturdays.
(U shanba kunlari xarid qilgani boradi.)

q.uz: U shanba kunlari xarid qilgani boradi.

q.q: Do you want to go ___ ? It's hot today. (swim)
They went ___ a trip to Khiva.
We went ___ a drink after work.
I'd like to go ___ in the mountains this winter. (ski)
q.uz: Bu qish tog'da chang'i uchgani borishni xohlayman.

intro:
Go fe'li har xil predloglar bilan har xil iboralar yasaydi:
• go to + joy: go to work, go to the bank
• go on: go on holiday, go on a trip
• go for: go for a walk, go for a swim
• go + -ing (sport, faoliyat): go shopping, go swimming
explain:
1. Iboralar jadvali

IboraMisollar
go to + joygo to school, go to the cinema, go to bed
go ongo on holiday, go on a trip, go on a tour
go forgo for a walk, go for a run, go for a drink, go for a swim
go + -inggo shopping, go swimming, go fishing, go skiing, go running

2. Misollar

• We went on holiday to Turkey. (Ta'tilga Turkiyaga bordik.)
• Let's go for a walk. (Sayr qilgani chiqaylik.)
• She goes shopping on Saturdays. (U shanba kunlari xarid qilgani boradi.)
• My father went fishing yesterday. (Otam kecha baliq ovlagani bordi.)

3. Diqqat

• go home — to siz!
• go + -ing bilan to ishlatilmaydi: go swimming (not go to swimming).
tip: O'zbekchadagi "…gani bormoq" (xarid qilgani, suzgani) ko'pincha go + -ing bo'ladi: go shopping, go swimming. "Sayrga chiqmoq" = go for a walk.
ex: I go to the gym three times a week.
Haftada uch marta sport zaliga boraman.
They're going on a trip to Khiva.
Do you want to go for a coffee?
We went swimming in the lake.
My mother goes shopping every Sunday.
Onam har yakshanba xarid qilgani boradi.

title: get
lesson:
get ko'p ma'noli fe'l:
get + narsa = olmoq: I got a letter.
(Xat oldim.)
get + sifat = bo'lib qolmoq: It's getting dark.
(Qorong'i tushyapti.)
get to / get home = yetib bormoq: I got home at 10.
(Uyga soat 10 da yetib keldim.)
get up = turmoq · get married = turmush qurmoq
get on/off (bus) · get in/out of (car)

q.q: What time did you ___ home last night?
q.uz: Kecha kechqurun uyga soat nechada yetib keldingiz?

q.q: Get ___ the bus at the next stop.
I ___ a message from Ali this morning. (get — past)
She got ___ the car and drove away.
How do you ___ to work? — By metro.

intro:
Get — ingliz tilidagi eng ko'p ma'noli fe'llardan biri. Uning ma'nosi keyingi so'zga qarab o'zgaradi:
• get + narsa = olmoq: I got a letter.
• get + sifat = bo'lib qolmoq: It's getting dark.
• get + joy = yetib bormoq: I got home at 6.
explain:
1. Asosiy ma'nolari

2. Transport bilan

• get on / get off — avtobus, poyezd, samolyot: Get off at the next stop.
• get in / get out of — mashina, taksi: She got into the taxi.

3. Shakllari

get — got — got (Amerikada gotten)
• It's getting cold. (Sovuq tushyapti.)
• I got home late. (Uyga kech yetib keldim.)
tip: O'zbekchada get ning har bir ma'nosi uchun alohida so'z bor: olmoq, bo'lib qolmoq, yetib kelmoq, turmoq. Inglizchada esa bularning hammasi bitta get bilan aytiladi, faqat yonidagi so'zga qarang.
ex: I got a message from my teacher.
What time did you get home?
My sister is getting married next week.
Get off the bus at the museum.
I always get hungry in the evening.

title: do and make
lesson:
do — ish, faoliyat: do homework, do housework, do the shopping, do an exam, do exercise, do your best
make — yaratish, yasash: make a cake, make tea, make a mistake, make a noise, make a phone call, make a decision, make money

• I did my homework.
(Uy vazifamni qildim.)
• Don't make a noise.
(Shovqin qilmang.)

I ___ a mistake in the test.
Who ___ the shopping in your family?
I need to ___ a phone call.
You should ___ some exercise every day.
q.uz: Har kuni biroz mashq qilishingiz kerak.

q.q: We have to ___ a decision today.

Do va make — ikkalasi ham o'zbekchaga ko'pincha "qilmoq" deb tarjima qilinadi, lekin ular farq qiladi:
• do — ish, faoliyat, vazifa bajarish: do homework, do the shopping
• make — yaratish, yasash, tayyorlash: make tea, make a cake, make a mistake
explain:
1. do — faoliyat

3. Eslab qolish usuli

Natijada yangi narsa paydo bo'lsa (choy, tort, shovqin, xato) → make. Shunchaki ish bajarilsa → do.
tip: O'zbekchada ikkalasi ham "qilmoq". Shuning uchun iboralarni butunligicha yodlang: do homework, make a mistake, make tea.

Can you make me a cup of tea?
Menga bir piyola choy damlab bera olasizmi?
She does the shopping on Saturdays.

title: have
lesson:
have ko'p iboralarda "qilmoq" ma'nosida:
have breakfast/lunch/dinner · have a shower · have a rest · have a party · have a good time · have a look

• I usually have breakfast at 7.
(Odatda soat 7 da nonushta qilaman.)
• Have a good time!
(Yaxshi dam oling!)

⚠️ Bu ma'noda continuous mumkin: She's having a shower.
("egalik" ma'nosida emas: I'm having a car ✗)

q.q: ___ a good time at the party!
Can I ___ a look at your photos?
You look tired. You should ___ a rest.
I ___ a car. (= I own a car)

intro:
Have faqat "egalik" (bor) ma'nosida emas, ko'p iboralarda "qilmoq" ma'nosida ham ishlatiladi:
• have breakfast — nonushta qilmoq
• have a shower — dush qabul qilmoq
• have a good time — yaxshi vaqt o'tkazmoq
explain:
1. have + ot — harakat ma'nosida

2. Muhim farq

Harakat ma'nosida -ing shakli mumkin:
• She's having a shower. (U dush qabul qilyapti.) ✅
Egalik ma'nosida -ing mumkin emas:
• I have a car. ✅ · I'm having a car. ❌

3. Savol va inkor

Harakat ma'nosida doim do/does/did bilan:
• What time do you have lunch? · I didn't have breakfast.
tip: O'zbekchada "nonushta qilmoq", "dush qabul qilmoq", "dam olmoq" deymiz. Inglizchada bularning hammasi have bilan aytiladi.
ex: Biz soat 7 da kechki ovqat qilamiz.
Did you have a good time at the wedding?

Can I have a look at your photos?
I didn't have breakfast this morning.

title: I / me · he / him · they / them
lesson:
Ega: I · you · he · she · it · we · they
To'ldiruvchi: me · you · him · her · it · us · them

• I know her. She knows me.
(Men uni taniyman. U meni taniydi.)
• Call us tomorrow.
(Ertaga bizga qo'ng'iroq qiling.)
• Give it to them.
(Buni ularga bering.)

q.uz: Men Sarani taniyman. Uni yaxshi bilaman.

q.q: Ali and I are friends. ___ go to the same school.
q.uz: Ali va men do'stmiz. Biz bir maktabga boramiz.

Biz uydamiz. Keyinroq bizga qo'ng'iroq qiling.

q.q: My parents live in Bukhara. I visit ___ every month.
q.uz: Ota-onam Buxoroda yashaydi. Ularni har oy ko'rgani boraman.

intro:
Ingliz tilida olmoshlar ikki shaklda keladi:
• Ega shakli (kim?): I, you, he, she, it, we, they
• To'ldiruvchi shakli (kimni? kimga?): me, you, him, her, it, us, them

She knows me. (U meni taniydi.) · I know her. (Men uni taniyman.)
explain:

2. Qachon qaysi biri?

• Fe'ldan oldin (ish qiluvchi) → ega shakli: He works. They live here.
• Fe'ldan keyin → to'ldiruvchi shakli: Call me. I love them.

Men Lolani yoqtiraman. U juda mehribon.
Where are my glasses? I can't find them.
We went to the cinema with them.
This is my father. He is a doctor.

title: my / his / their etc.
lesson:
I → my · you → your · he → his · she → her
it → its · we → our · they → their

• This is my brother. His name is Ali.
(Bu mening akam. Uning ismi Ali.)
• They love their children.
(Ular farzandlarini yaxshi ko'radi.)

⚠️ its (uning — narsa/hayvon) · it's = it is

q.uz: Bu mening akam. Uning ismi Ali.

q.q: This is my sister. ___ name is Lola.
q.uz: Bu mening singlim. Uning ismi Lola.

q.q: Is this ___ bag? — Yes, it's mine.
I'm Tom and this is ___ wife.

Bu mavzuda egalik olmoshlarini o'rganamiz: my (mening), your (sening/sizning), his (uning — erkak), her (uning — ayol), its (uning — narsa), our (bizning), their (ularning).

Ular doim otdan oldin keladi: my book, her car, their house.

1. Jadval

OlmoshEgalikMisol

Egasiga qarang, narsaga emas!

3. its va it's

• it's = it is: It's raining.

title: Whose is this? It's mine / yours / hers
lesson:
my → mine · your → yours · his → his · her → hers
our → ours · their → theirs

Otdan keyin emas, o'zi yolg'iz ishlatiladi:
• This is my bag. → This bag is mine.
(Bu sumka meniki.)
• Whose is this phone? — It's hers.
(Bu telefon kimniki? — Uniki.)
• a friend of mine
(do'stlarimdan biri)

q.q: Is this your pen? — Yes, it's ___ .
These aren't our keys. ___ are on the table.
q.uz: Bular bizning kalitlarimiz emas. Biznikilar stol ustida.

q.q: That car belongs to my parents. It's ___.
Is this Lola's book? — Yes, it's ___.
Is this umbrella ___ ? — No, it isn't mine.
q.uz: Bu soyabon siznikimi? — Yo'q, meniki emas.

intro:
Bu mavzuda "meniki, seniki, uniki" degan so'zlarni o'rganamiz: mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs.

Ular otsiz, yolg'iz ishlatiladi:
This is my book. → This book is mine. (Bu kitob meniki.)
Whose is this? — It's hers. (Bu kimniki? — Uniki.)
explain:
1. Jadval

Otdan oldinYolg'iz (otsiz)Tarjima
myminemeniki
youryoursseniki / sizniki
hishisuniki (erkak)
herhersuniki (ayol)
ouroursbizniki
theirtheirsularniki

2. Qachon qaysi biri?

• Keyin ot kelsa → my, your, her…: my car, her bag
• Keyin ot kelmasa → mine, yours, hers…: The car is mine.

3. Whose? — Kimniki?

• Whose phone is this? / Whose is this phone? (Bu telefon kimniki?)
• It's mine. / It's Ali's.

4. a friend of mine

"Do'stlarimdan biri" = a friend of mine (not a friend of me)
tip: O'zbekchadagi "-niki" qo'shimchasi (meniki, uniki, bizniki) = mine, his/hers, ours. "Kimniki?" = Whose?
ex: This pen isn't mine. Is it yours?
Whose car is that? — It's theirs.
Lola's bag is red. Hers is the red one.
Our flat is small, but theirs is big.
Bizning kvartiramiz kichik, ularniki esa katta.
Is this umbrella yours or his?

title: I / me / my / mine
lesson:
I · me · my · mine
you · you · your · yours
he · him · his · his
she · her · her · hers
we · us · our · ours
they · them · their · theirs

• I gave my book to him. Now it's his.
(Men kitobimni unga berdim. Endi u uniki.)

q.q: Where are Ali's shoes? — ___ shoes are here. (he)
q.uz: Alining tuflisi qayerda? — Uning tuflisi shu yerda.

q.q: We know them, and they know ___.
q.uz: Biz ularni taniymiz, ular ham bizni taniydi.

intro:
Bu mavzu — olmoshlarni takrorlash. Har bir shaxs uchun to'rtta shakl bor va ularni adashtirmaslik kerak:
I (men) → me (meni/menga) → my (mening) → mine (meniki)

I gave my book to him. Now it's his.
explain:
1. To'liq jadval

EgaTo'ldiruvchiEgalik + otEgalik (otsiz)
Imemymine
youyouyouryours
hehimhishis
sheherherhers
ititits—
weusourours
theythemtheirtheirs

2. Qanday tanlash

• Fe'ldan oldin, ish qiluvchi → I, he, they
• Fe'l yoki predlogdan keyin → me, him, them
• Ot oldidan → my, his, their
• Ot o'rniga → mine, his, theirs

3. Bitta gapda

We invited them to our house, and they invited us to theirs.
tip: O'zbekchadagi qo'shimchalarga qarab tanlang: men → I, meni/menga → me, mening → my, meniki → mine.
ex: I called her, but she didn't answer me.
Unga qo'ng'iroq qildim, lekin u menga javob bermadi.
Is this book yours or mine?
He told us about his trip.
U bizga sayohati haqida gapirib berdi.
Give it to me. It's mine!

title: myself / yourself / themselves
lesson:
myself · yourself · himself · herself · itself · ourselves · yourselves · themselves

Ega va to'ldiruvchi bir shaxs bo'lsa:
• I cut myself.
(O'zimni kesib oldim.)
by myself = yolg'iz, o'zim:
• She lives by herself.
(U yolg'iz yashaydi.)

each other = bir-birini: They love each other.
(Ular bir-birini yaxshi ko'radi.)

q.q: I cut ___ while I was cooking.

q.uz: Ali va Lola bir-birini yaxshi ko'radi.

q.q: He taught ___ to play the guitar.

intro:
Bu mavzuda o'zlik olmoshlarini o'rganamiz: myself (o'zimni), yourself (o'zingizni), himself, herself, ourselves, themselves.

Ular ish bajaruvchining o'ziga qaytganda ishlatiladi:
I cut myself. (O'zimni kesib oldim.)
explain:
1. Jadval

EgaO'zlik olmoshi
Imyself
youyourself (birlik) / yourselves (ko'plik)
he / she / ithimself / herself / itself
weourselves
theythemselves

2. Qachon ishlatiladi?

• Ish o'ziga qaytsa: She looked at herself in the mirror. (U ko'zguda o'ziga qaradi.)
• "O'zi, boshqa birovsiz": I made this cake myself. (Bu tortni o'zim qildim.)
• by myself = yolg'iz: He lives by himself. (U yolg'iz yashaydi.)
• enjoy yourself — yaxshi dam oling: Enjoy yourselves!

3. each other — bir-birini

• They love each other. (Ular bir-birini yaxshi ko'radi.)
• They love themselves. (Ular o'zlarini yaxshi ko'radi.) — butunlay boshqa ma'no!
tip: O'zbekchadagi "o'zim, o'zini, o'zlari" = myself, himself, themselves. "Bir-birini" esa = each other.
ex: She taught herself to play the guitar.
I don't like going to the cinema by myself.
Ali and Vali help each other.
Ali va Vali bir-biriga yordam beradi.
Did you enjoy yourselves at the party?
mi: We met each other at school.
She lives by her own self.

title: -'s (Kate's camera / my brother's car)
lesson:
Odam yoki hayvonga tegishlilik: -'s
• Kate's camera
(Keytning fotoapparati)
• my brother's car
(akamning mashinasi)

Ko'plik -s bilan tugasa — faqat ': my parents' house
(ota-onamning uyi)
Lekin: the children's toys, the men's room

Narsalar uchun ko'pincha of: the name of the street

q.q: This is the car of my brother. → This is my ___ car.
Is this Ali's phone? — No, it's ___ . (Lola)
Who is that? — It's my ___ husband. (sister)

intro:
Bu mavzuda kimgadir tegishlilikni bildirishni o'rganamiz: "Keytning fotoapparati", "akamning mashinasi".

Ingliz tilida buning uchun ismga 's qo'shiladi:
Kate's camera (Keytning fotoapparati) · my brother's car (akamning mashinasi)
explain:
1. Qoidalar

HolatQoidaMisol
Birlik+ 'smy sister's room
-s bilan tugaydigan ko'plik+ 'my parents' house
Noto'g'ri ko'plik+ 'sthe children's toys, men's clothes

2. Qachon 's, qachon of?

• Odam va hayvonlar uchun ko'pincha 's: Ali's phone, the dog's bed
• Narsalar uchun ko'pincha of: the name of the street, the end of the film
"the street's name" emas, the name of the street.

3. Ot tushib qolishi mumkin

• Is this Ali's phone? — No, it's Lola's. (… Yo'q, Lolaniki.)
• I stayed at my aunt's. (Xolamnikida qoldim.)
tip: O'zbekchadagi "-ning" qo'shimchasi (Alining, akamning) odamlar uchun inglizchada 's bo'ladi: Ali's, my brother's. Tartib ham bir xil: egasi oldin, narsa keyin.
ex: My parents' house is in Fergana.
What's the name of this street?
We had dinner at my grandmother's.
mi: This is the car of my father.

title: a / an
lesson:
a + undosh tovush: a car, a book, a university (yu-)
an + unli tovush: an apple, an hour (h o'qilmaydi), an umbrella

Kasb aytishda: She's a doctor.
(U shifokor.)
Birinchi marta tilga olinganda: I bought a new phone.
(Yangi telefon sotib oldim.)

q.q: I bought ___ new car last week.

intro:
A / an — noaniq artikl. Ma'nosi "bitta, qandaydir bir". U faqat sanaladigan birlik otlar oldidan keladi: a book, an apple.

• a — undosh tovush oldidan: a car, a dog
• an — unli tovush oldidan: an apple, an egg
explain:
1. a yoki an — tovushga qarang!

Harfga emas, o'qilishiga qarang:
aan
a book, a caran apple, an orange
a university (yu-)an umbrella (a-)
a European (yu-)an hour (h o'qilmaydi)
a house (h o'qiladi)an honest man

2. Qachon ishlatiladi?

• Birinchi marta tilga olinganda: I saw a cat. (Bir mushuk ko'rdim.)
• Kasb: She's a teacher. (U o'qituvchi.) — inglizchada a shart!
• Biror narsa nima ekanini aytganda: It's an old house. (Bu eski uy.)
• "Bitta" ma'nosida: I'll be back in an hour.

3. Ishlatilmaydi

• Ko'plik bilan: books (not a books)
• Sanalmaydigan bilan: water, money (not a water)
tip: O'zbekchada "U o'qituvchi" deymiz, artikl yo'q. Inglizchada kasbdan oldin a/an shart: She's a teacher. "She's teacher" — eng ko'p uchraydigan xato.
ex: She studies at a university in Tashkent.

title: train(s) / bus(es) (singular and plural)
lesson:
Odatda -s: book → books, car → cars
-es: bus → buses, box → boxes, watch → watches
-y → -ies: city → cities (lekin day → days)
-f → -ves: knife → knives, wife → wives

Noto'g'ri: man → men, woman → women, child → children, foot → feet, tooth → teeth, person → people, mouse → mice

Doim ko'plik: trousers, jeans, glasses, scissors

q.q: There were a lot of ___ at the concert.

intro:
Bu mavzuda otlarning ko'plik shaklini o'rganamiz. O'zbekchada ko'plik uchun "-lar" qo'shamiz, inglizchada esa ko'pincha -s yoki -es qo'shiladi:
book → books, bus → buses

Lekin ba'zi otlar butunlay o'zgaradi: man → men, child → children.
explain:
1. Qoidalar

QoidaMisol
Odatda + scar → cars, day → days
-s, -sh, -ch, -x → + esbus → buses, dish → dishes, watch → watches, box → boxes
undosh + y → iescity → cities, baby → babies
-f / -fe → vesknife → knives, wife → wives, leaf → leaves

2. Noto'g'ri ko'plik — yodlang!

BirlikKo'plik
man / womanmen / women
childchildren
personpeople
foot / toothfeet / teeth
mousemice
fish / sheepfish / sheep (o'zgarmaydi)

3. Doim ko'plik

trousers, jeans, shorts, glasses, scissors — ikki qismli narsalar, doim ko'plik fe'l bilan: My jeans are new.
tip: O'zbekchada son bilan ko'plik qo'shimchasi ishlatilmaydi: "uchta kitob". Inglizchada esa son bilan ham -s shart: three books.
ex: There are three buses to the city.
Many people live in big cities.
Brush your teeth twice a day.
My glasses are on the table.

title: a bottle / some water (countable / uncountable 1)
lesson:
Sanaladigan: a book, two books, a banana
Sanalmaydigan: water, money, rice, bread, music, information, advice, furniture
— a/an va ko'plik -s olmaydi!

• I need some water. (not a water)
(Menga biroz suv kerak.)
• a bottle of water · a piece of bread · a cup of tea
(bir shisha suv · bir bo'lak non · bir piyola choy)

q.q: I'd like a ___ of tea, please.
Can I have a ___ of bread?

intro:
Ingliz tilida otlar ikki turga bo'linadi:
• Sanaladigan (countable) — bitta, ikkita deb sanasa bo'ladi: a book, two books
• Sanalmaydigan (uncountable) — sanab bo'lmaydi: water, money, rice, bread, advice, information

Sanalmaydigan otlar bilan a/an ishlatilmaydi va -s qo'shilmaydi!
explain:
1. Farqlar

SanaladiganSanalmaydigan
a car, two carswater (not a water, waters)
a banana, bananasbread, rice, sugar, milk
a jobwork
a suggestionadvice
a chair, a tablefurniture

2. Diqqat! O'zbekchada sanaladigan, inglizchada esa sanalmaydigan otlar

advice (maslahat), information (ma'lumot), furniture (mebel), news (yangilik), homework, luggage (yuk), money
• She gave me some advice. (not an advice, advices)
• The news is good. (not are)

3. Qanday sanash mumkin?

a … of bilan:
a bottle of water · a piece of bread · a cup of tea · a glass of milk · a piece of advice · a kilo of rice
tip: O'zbekchada "bitta maslahat", "ikkita ma'lumot" deymiz. Inglizchada esa advice va information sanalmaydi: some advice, a piece of information.
ex: Can I have a glass of water?
I need some information about the trains.
He gave me some good advice.
I'd like a piece of cake.
mi: Can you give me an advice?
Can you give me some advice?

title: a cake / some cake / some cakes (countable / uncountable 2)
lesson:
a/an + birlik sanaladigan: a cake (butun tort)
some + ko'plik: some cakes (bir nechta tort)
some + sanalmaydigan: some cake (tortdan bir qism)

• Would you like some coffee?
(Qahva ichasizmi?)
• I bought some apples.
(Olma sotib oldim.)
• We need some new chairs.
(Bizga yangi stullar kerak.)

q.q: I bought ___ apples at the market.

q.uz: Bizga bir nechta yangi stul kerak.

q.q: Can I have ___ cake? Just a small piece.
q.uz: Tortdan bir oz olsam bo'ladimi? Kichkina bo'lak.

intro:
Ba'zi otlar ham sanaladigan, ham sanalmaydigan bo'lishi mumkin, ma'nosi biroz o'zgaradi:
• a cake — butun bitta tort
• some cake — tortdan bir bo'lak (sanalmaydigan ma'noda)
• some cakes — bir nechta tort

Bu mavzuda a/an va some ni qachon ishlatishni o'rganamiz.
explain:
1. Asosiy qoida

Ot turiArtikl/so'zMisol
Sanaladigan birlika / ana sandwich, an egg
Sanaladigan ko'pliksomesome apples
Sanalmaydigansomesome milk, some music

2. Ma'no farqi

• I'd like a coffee. — bitta piyola qahva (kafeda)
• I'd like some coffee. — biroz qahva
• a chicken — tirik tovuq · some chicken — tovuq go'shti
• a paper — gazeta · some paper — qog'oz

3. Umumiy gapda — hech narsa

• She has beautiful hair. (sanalmaydi, artiklsiz) (Uning sochlari chiroyli.)
• I like music.
tip: O'zbekchadagi "biroz, bir oz" (biroz suv, bir oz tort) ko'pincha some bo'ladi. "Bitta" esa a/an.
ex: I had an egg for breakfast.
Can I have some cake? Just a small piece.
Tortdan biroz olsam bo'ladimi? Kichkina bo'lak.

title: a / an and the
lesson:
a/an — birinchi marta, qaysiligi noma'lum
the — qaysi ekanligi aniq, ilgari aytilgan, yagona

• I saw a dog. The dog was very big.
(Bir it ko'rdim. It juda katta edi.)
• Can you close the door, please?
(Eshikni yopib qo'ya olasizmi?)
• the sun · the moon · the sky

q.q: I saw ___ dog in the park. ___ dog was very big.
q.uz: Bog'da bir it ko'rdim. It juda katta edi.
q.w: Birinchi marta → a, ikkinchi marta → The.

q.q: I have ___ brother and a sister.
q.uz: Mening bitta akam va bitta opam bor.

q.q: She bought a dress and a hat. ___ dress was red.
q.uz: U ko'ylak va shlyapa sotib oldi. Ko'ylak qizil edi.

intro:
Bu mavzuda a/an (noaniq artikl) va the (aniq artikl) farqini o'rganamiz:
• a / an — qandaydir bir, birinchi marta aytilmoqda
• the — o'sha, ma'lum, ikkala tomon ham qaysi biri ekanini biladi

I saw a dog. The dog was very big. (Bir it ko'rdim. O'sha it juda katta edi.)
explain:
1. Asosiy farq

a / anthe
Birinchi martaIkkinchi marta / ma'lum
Qaysi biri muhim emasAynan o'sha
I bought a shirt.The shirt is blue.

2. the — qachon?

• Avval aytilgan: I have a cat and a dog. The cat is black.
• Qaysi biri ekani aniq (vaziyatdan): Close the door, please. (xonada bitta eshik)
• Dunyoda yagona: the sun, the moon, the sky, the world
• Bitta joyda bitta: the kitchen, the bathroom, the station

3. Solishtiring

• Is there a bank near here? — qaysidir bank
• Where's the bank? — o'sha biz biladigan bank
tip: O'zbek tilida artikl yo'q, shuning uchun bu mavzu qiyin. Oddiy qoida: agar "o'sha" deb aytish mumkin bo'lsa — the; "bir, qandaydir" bo'lsa — a/an.
ex: I bought a book and a pen. The book was cheap.
Kitob va ruchka sotib oldim. Kitob arzon edi.
Can you turn off the light?
We stayed in a hotel. The hotel was near the sea.
Biz mehmonxonada qoldik. Mehmonxona dengiz yaqinida edi.
She has a son and a daughter.
Uning bir o'g'li va bir qizi bor.

title: the ...
lesson:
the ishlatiladi: the same, the first/second, the cinema, the theatre, the radio, the sea, the internet
• in the morning / afternoon / evening

the ishlatilmaydi: TV (watch TV), breakfast/lunch/dinner, next/last week
• at night · at home · at work

• I watch TV in the evening.
(Kechqurun televizor ko'raman.)
• We went to the cinema last week.
(O'tgan hafta kinoga bordik.)

q.q: I usually watch ___ TV in the evening.
What did you have for ___ breakfast?
I always go for a walk in ___ morning.
She was ___ first person to arrive.

intro:
Bu mavzuda the qachon kerak va qachon kerak emasligini o'rganamiz. Ba'zi iboralarda the doim bor, ba'zilarida esa hech qachon yo'q.

✅ in the morning, go to the cinema, the same
❌ watch TV, have breakfast, next week, at night
explain:
1. the bilan

IboraMisol

the first / the lastHe was the first.
in the morning / afternoon / eveningI work in the morning.
the cinema / the theatrego to the cinema
the radio / the internetlisten to the radio

2. the siz

IboraMisol

breakfast / lunch / dinnerhave lunch
