at night / at home / at workI'm at home.
tip: Bu iboralarni qoidadan ko'ra butunligicha yodlash osonroq: "in the morning", "watch TV", "have lunch", "next week".
ex: I always drink coffee in the morning.
Did you watch TV last night?
Let's go to the cinema on Friday.
What did you have for lunch?
mi: I watch the TV every evening.

title: go to work / go home / go to the cinema
lesson:
the siz: go to work, go to school, go to university, go to bed, go to hospital, go home (to siz!)
the bilan: go to the cinema, the bank, the station, the doctor, the shop

• I go to work by bus.
(Ishga avtobusda boraman.)
• It's late. Let's go home.
(Kech bo'ldi. Uyga ketaylik.)
• I need to go to the bank.
(Bankka borishim kerak.)

q.q: I need to go to ___ bank.
What time do you go to ___ ?
My son is 7. He goes to ___ now. (maktab)
I have a toothache. I must go to ___ dentist.
q.uz: Tishim og'riyapti. Tish shifokoriga borishim kerak.

intro:
Ba'zi joylar bilan the ishlatilmaydi, chunki biz o'sha joyning asosiy vazifasi haqida gapiramiz:
go to work, go to school, go to bed, go home.

Boshqa joylar bilan esa the kerak: go to the bank, the cinema, the station.
explain:
1. the siz

IboraTarjima
go to work / be at workishga bormoq / ishda bo'lmoq
go to school / universitymaktabga / universitetga bormoq (o'qish uchun)
go to bed / be in beduxlashga yotmoq / to'shakda bo'lmoq
go to hospital / prisonkasalxonaga / qamoqqa tushmoq
go home / be at homeuyga bormoq (to ham yo'q!)

2. the bilan

go to the bank · the post office · the station · the airport · the cinema · the doctor · the dentist · the shop

3. Ma'no farqi

• My son goes to school. — u o'quvchi, o'qish uchun boradi.
• I went to the school to see the teacher. — binoga bordim (o'qish uchun emas).
tip: Eng ko'p xato: "go to home". To'g'risi: go home, come home, get home — to ham, the ham yo'q.
ex: What time do you go to work?
The children are at school now.
I'm tired. I'm going to bed.
I need to go to the bank.
She's in hospital after the accident.
mi: I go to the work by bus.
I go to work by bus.

title: I like music · I hate exams
lesson:
Umuman gapirganda the ishlatilmaydi:
• I like music.
(Musiqani yoqtiraman.)
• Dogs are friendly animals.
(Itlar do'stona hayvonlar.)
• Life is short.
(Hayot qisqa.)

Aniq narsa haqida — the:
• The music at the party was loud.
(Ziyofatdagi musiqa baland edi.)

q.q: ___ music at the party was very loud.
___ vegetables in this shop are very fresh.
Can you pass me ___ salt, please?

intro:
Biror narsa haqida umuman gapirganda the ishlatilmaydi:
I like music. (Musiqani yoqtiraman — umuman, har qanday musiqani.)
Dogs are friendly. (Itlar do'stona — umuman barcha itlar.)

Aniq narsa haqida gapirganda esa the kerak:
The music at the party was loud. (Ziyofatdagi musiqa baland edi.)
explain:
1. Umumiy — the siz

TuriMisol
Ko'plik otlarCats like milk. I hate exams.
Sanalmaydigan otlarMoney isn't everything. I love music.
Fanlar, sport, tillarI study history. He plays football. She speaks English.
Ovqatlar, ichimliklarI don't drink coffee.

2. Aniq — the bilan

• I like the music in this film. (Bu filmdagi musiqa menga yoqadi.)
• The vegetables from our garden are fresh. (Bog'imizdagi sabzavotlar yangi.)
• Pass me the salt, please. (stol ustidagi aniq tuz)

3. Solishtiring

• Life is beautiful. — umuman hayot
• The life of Navoi was interesting. — aniq bir odamning hayoti
tip: O'zbek tilida bu farq yo'q. Oddiy test: "umuman, hamma" degan ma'no bo'lsa → the yo'q. "aynan shu, o'sha" degan ma'no bo'lsa → the.
ex: The children in my class are very clever.
The film we watched yesterday was great.

title: the ... (names of places)
lesson:
the siz: mamlakatlar (Uzbekistan, France), shaharlar, qit'alar (Asia), ko'llar, tog'lar (Everest), ko'chalar
the bilan: the USA, the UK, the Netherlands · daryolar (the Amudarya), dengizlar, okeanlar (the Atlantic), cho'llar (the Sahara), tog' tizmalari (the Alps)
Mehmonxona, muzey, teatr: the Hilton, the British Museum

q.q: ___ Tashkent is the capital of Uzbekistan.

intro:
Bu mavzuda joy nomlari bilan the qachon kerakligini o'rganamiz.

Ko'pchilik nomlar the siz: Uzbekistan, Tashkent, Asia, Everest.
Lekin ba'zilari the bilan: the USA, the Amudarya, the Atlantic, the Alps.

tip: Eslab qolish uchun: suv (daryo, dengiz, okean) va ko'plik nomlar (tog' tizmasi, orollar, the USA) — the bilan. Bitta joy (shahar, mamlakat, bitta tog') — the siz.
ex: The Syrdarya flows into the Aral Sea.
The Kyzylkum is a big desert.
We visited the Louvre in Paris.

title: this / that / these / those
lesson:
Yaqin: this (birlik) · these (ko'plik)
Uzoq: that (birlik) · those (ko'plik)

• This is my phone.
(Bu mening telefonim.)
• Look at those birds!
(Anavi qushlarga qarang!)
• Who's that man?
(Anavi odam kim?)
• That's a good idea!
(Bu yaxshi fikr!)

q.q: Look at ___ birds in the sky!
___ shoes are very comfortable. (I'm wearing them)
I'll have pizza. — ___ a good idea!
___ are my children, Ali and Lola. (here, near me)
q.uz: Bular mening farzandlarim, Ali va Lola.

q.q: Hello, ___ is Ali speaking. (on the phone)

intro:
Bu mavzuda ko'rsatish olmoshlarini o'rganamiz:
• this — bu (yaqindagi bitta narsa) · these — bular (yaqindagi ko'p narsa)
• that — u, anavi (uzoqdagi bitta) · those — ular, anavilar (uzoqdagi ko'p)
explain:
1. Jadval

BirlikKo'plik
Yaqin (shu yerda)this bookthese books
Uzoq (u yerda)that bookthose books

2. Ot bilan va otsiz

• This phone is new. (ot bilan)
• This is my phone. (otsiz)
• Who are those people? · Those are my friends.

3. Maxsus ishlatilishi

• Telefonda: Hello, this is Ali. (Allo, bu Ali.) — "I am Ali" emas!
• Tanishtirishda: This is my sister, Lola. (Bu singlim Lola.)
• Fikrga javob: That's a good idea! · That's right. (To'g'ri.)
• Hozirgi vaqt: this morning, this week (bu hafta)

ex: I'll pay. — Thanks, that's very kind of you.

title: one / ones
lesson:
Otni takrorlamaslik uchun:
one — birlik · ones — ko'plik

• I don't like this shirt. I'll take the blue one.
(Bu ko'ylak yoqmadi. Ko'k rangdagisini olaman.)
• These shoes are old. I need new ones.
(Bu tuflilar eski. Menga yangilari kerak.)
• Which one? · Which ones?
(Qaysi biri? · Qaysilari?)

q.q: I don't like this shirt. I'll take the blue ___ .
q.uz: Bu ko'ylak yoqmadi. Ko'k rangdagisini olaman.

q.q: These shoes are old. I need new ___ .
q.uz: Bu tuflilar eski. Menga yangilari kerak.

q.q: Which ___ do you want, the big one or the small one?
q.uz: Qaysi birini xohlaysiz, kattasinimi yoki kichigini?

q.q: I need a pen. Have you got ___ ?
Those apples are bad. Take these ___ . They're fresh.
q.uz: Anavi olmalar yomon. Bularini oling. Yangi.

q.q: Which ___ are yours? — The black ones.
My car is old. I want a new ___ .
This cup is dirty. Can I have a clean ___ ?
q.uz: Bu piyola kir. Tozasini bera olasizmi?

intro:
One / ones — otni takrorlamaslik uchun ishlatiladi:
• one — birlik o'rniga: I don't like this shirt. I'll take the blue one. (…ko'kini olaman.)
• ones — ko'plik o'rniga: These shoes are old. I need new ones. (…yangilari kerak.)
explain:
1. Qachon ishlatiladi?

Ot avval aytilgan va qaysi narsa haqida gap ketayotgani tushunarli bo'lganda:
• Which bag is yours? — The black one. (Qaysi sumka sizniki? — Qorasi.)
• I like these apples, but not those ones.

2. Turli shakllar

ShaklMisolTarjima
a / an + sifat + onea big onekattasi
the + sifat + one(s)the red onesqizillari
Which one(s)?Which one?Qaysi biri?

3. Sifatsiz "a … one"

• I need a pen. Have you got one? (Menga ruchka kerak. Sizda bormi?)
Bu yerda one = a pen.

4. Sanalmaydigan otlar bilan ishlatilmaydi

I don't want white bread, I want brown (bread). — "brown one" emas.
tip: O'zbekchadagi "-i / -lari" qo'shimchasi (qizili, kattasi, yangilari) inglizchada one / ones bilan aytiladi: the red one, new ones.
ex: Which car is yours? — The white one.
These glasses are dirty. Can I have clean ones?
Bu stakanlar kir. Tozalarini bera olasizmi?
I want a phone like this one.
My bike is old. I need a new one.
Do you have a map? — Yes, I've got one.
mi: I want a water cold one.

title: some and any
lesson:
some — ijobiy gaplarda, taklif va iltimosda:
• I've got some money.
(Biroz pulim bor.)
• Would you like some tea?

any — inkor va savolda:
• I haven't got any money.
(Umuman pulim yo'q.)
• Are there any shops near here?
(Bu yer yaqinida do'konlar bormi?)

q.q: There aren't ___ eggs in the fridge.
Have you got ___ brothers or sisters?

intro:
Some va any — ikkalasi ham "biroz, bir nechta, qandaydir" degan ma'noni beradi, lekin har xil gaplarda ishlatiladi:
• some — ijobiy gaplarda: I have some money.
• any — inkor va savol gaplarda: I don't have any money. Do you have any money?
explain:
1. Asosiy qoida

Gap turiSo'zMisol
Ijobiy (+)someThere are some eggs.
Inkor (−)anyThere aren't any eggs.
Savol (?)anyAre there any eggs?

2. Istisno: taklif va iltimosda — some

Javob "ha" bo'lishini kutsak, savolda ham some:
• Would you like some tea? (Choy ichasizmi?) — taklif
• Can I have some water? (Biroz suv bera olasizmi?) — iltimos

3. Qaysi otlar bilan?

some / any + ko'plik (some books) yoki sanalmaydigan (some milk).
Birlik bilan a/an: a book (not some book).
tip: O'zbekchada "biroz pulim bor" va "umuman pulim yo'q" deymiz. Inglizchada: ijobiyda some, inkorda any. Inkor gapda "any" so'zini "hech" deb tushunish mumkin.
ex: I bought some fruit at the market.
Are there any good restaurants here?
Can I ask you some questions?
Sizga bir nechta savol bersam bo'ladimi?
mi: There is an apple. / There are some apples.

title: not + any · no · none
lesson:
not … any = no + ot
• There aren't any shops. = There are no shops.
(Do'konlar yo'q.)

none — otsiz, yolg'iz ishlatiladi:
• How many children have they got? — None.
(Nechta farzandi bor? — Birorta ham yo'q.)

⚠️ Bitta inkor yetarli: There are no shops. (not There aren't no shops)

q.q: There aren't any shops here. = There are ___ shops here.
How much money have you got? — ___ .
I have ___ time today. I'm very busy.
q.uz: Bugun umuman vaqtim yo'q. Juda bandman.

q.q: There isn't ___ milk in the fridge.
I wanted some cake, but there was ___ left.
q.uz: Tort yemoqchi edim, lekin hech narsa qolmabdi.

q.q: We've got ___ bread. Can you buy some?
___ of my friends came to the party.

intro:
Bu mavzuda "yo'q, hech" ma'nosini bildirishning uch usulini o'rganamiz:
• not … any: There aren't any shops.
• no + ot: There are no shops. (bir xil ma'no)
• none — otsiz: How many shops are there? — None. (Birorta ham yo'q.)
explain:
1. not any = no

not … anyno
I don't have any money.I have no money.
There isn't any milk.There's no milk.
Ma'nosi bir xil. no biroz kuchliroq eshitiladi.

2. Bitta inkor yetarli!

• I have no time. ✅
• I don't have any time. ✅
• I don't have no time. ❌ (ikki inkor)

3. none

none — otsiz, yolg'iz ishlatiladi:
• How much money do you have? — None. (Umuman yo'q.)
• none of + ko'plik: None of my friends came. (Do'stlarimdan hech biri kelmadi.)
tip: O'zbekchada ikki inkor odatiy: "Hech kim kelmadi". Inglizchada esa bitta inkor yetarli: "Nobody came" yoki "I have no money" (don't + no — xato).
ex: There's no bread. Can you buy some?
There aren't any buses after midnight.
How many questions did you get wrong? — None!
Nechta savolga xato javob berdingiz? — Birortasiga ham!
None of the students knew the answer.

title: not + anybody / anything · nobody / nothing
lesson:
not … anybody/anyone = nobody/no-one (hech kim)
not … anything = nothing (hech narsa)

• I didn't see anybody. = I saw nobody.
(Hech kimni ko'rmadim.)
• She didn't say anything. = She said nothing.
(U hech narsa demadi.)
• Nobody called.
(Hech kim qo'ng'iroq qilmadi.)

q.uz: U hech narsa demadi. Jim edi.
Siz yo'qligingizda hech kim qo'ng'iroq qilmadi.

q.q: There's ___ in the box. It's empty.
What did you buy? — ___ . I didn't have any money.
q.uz: Nima sotib oldingiz? — Hech narsa. Pulim yo'q edi.
U kun bo'yi hech narsa yemadi.

q.q: Who was at home? — ___ . The house was empty.
q.uz: Uyda kim bor edi? — Hech kim. Uy bo'sh edi.

intro:
Bu mavzuda "hech kim" va "hech narsa" deyishni o'rganamiz:
• nobody / no-one = not … anybody — hech kim
• nothing = not … anything — hech narsa

I didn't see anybody. = I saw nobody. (Hech kimni ko'rmadim.)
explain:
1. Ikki usul

not + any-no- (fe'l ijobiy)Tarjima
I didn't see anybody.I saw nobody.Hech kimni ko'rmadim.
She didn't say anything.She said nothing.U hech narsa demadi.

2. Gap boshida — faqat nobody / nothing

• Nobody called. (Hech kim qo'ng'iroq qilmadi.) — "Anybody didn't call" ❌
• Nothing happened. (Hech narsa bo'lmadi.)

3. Qisqa javobda

• What did you buy? — Nothing.
• Who was there? — Nobody.

4. Bitta inkor!

O'zbekchada "Hech kimni ko'rmadim" — ikki inkor. Inglizchada bittasi:
❌ I didn't see nobody. ✅ I didn't see anybody. ✅ I saw nobody.
tip: O'zbekcha "hech kim … -ma-" inglizchaga ikki usulda o'tadi: fe'l inkor bo'lsa → anybody; fe'l ijobiy bo'lsa → nobody. Lekin hech qachon ikkalasi birga emas!
ex: U yerda biror kishi bormi? — Yo'q, hech kim.

title: somebody / anything / nowhere etc.
lesson:
somebody/someone — kimdir · something — nimadir · somewhere — qayerdadir
anybody · anything · anywhere — savol va inkorda
nobody · nothing · nowhere — hech kim, hech narsa, hech qayerda

• Somebody is at the door.
(Eshik oldida kimdir bor.)
• I want to go somewhere warm.
(Qayergadir issiq joyga borishni xohlayman.)
• Did you go anywhere?
(Biror joyga bordingizmi?)

q.q: ___ is at the door. Can you open it?
q.uz: Eshik oldida kimdir bor. Ochib bera olasizmi?
O'tgan dam olish kunlari biror joyga bordingizmi?

q.q: I'm hungry. I want ___ to eat.
I lost my keys. I can't find them ___ .
q.uz: Kalitlarimni yo'qotdim. Hech qayerdan topa olmayapman.

q.q: Is there ___ in the room? — No, it's empty.
q.uz: Xonada biror kishi bormi? — Yo'q, bo'sh.

q.q: There's ___ to sit. All the chairs are taken.
q.uz: O'tirishga joy yo'q. Hamma stullar band.

q.w: Taklif → something (savol bo'lgani uchun anything ham to'g'ri).

intro:
Bu mavzuda some-, any-, no-, every- bilan yasalgan so'zlarni o'rganamiz:
• somebody (kimdir), something (nimadir), somewhere (qayerdadir)
• anybody, anything, anywhere — savol va inkorda
• nobody, nothing, nowhere — hech kim, hech narsa, hech qayerda
explain:
1. Jadval

-body / -one (odam)-thing (narsa)-where (joy)
some- (+)somebodysomethingsomewhere
any- (? −)anybodyanythinganywhere
no-nobodynothingnowhere
every-everybodyeverythingeverywhere

2. some va any qoidasi xuddi Unit 76 dagidek

• Ijobiy: Somebody is at the door. (Eshik oldida kimdir bor.)
• Savol: Did you go anywhere? (Biror joyga bordingizmi?)
• Inkor: I can't find my keys anywhere. (Kalitlarimni hech qayerdan topa olmayapman.)
• Taklif: Would you like something to drink? (Biror narsa ichasizmi?)

3. Birlik fe'l

Bu so'zlar bilan fe'l birlikda: Everybody is here. Somebody has taken my pen.

4. + to + fe'l

something to eat (yeyishga biror narsa) · somewhere to sit (o'tirishga joy)
tip: O'zbekchadagi "-dir" (kimdir, nimadir, qayerdadir) = some-; "biror" (savolda) = any-; "hech" = no-.
ex: I want to go somewhere warm.
I've looked everywhere for my phone.
Would you like something to eat?

title: every and all
lesson:
every + birlik ot: every day, every student
• I go to the gym every day.
(Har kuni sport zaliga boraman.)

all + ko'plik yoki sanalmaydigan: all students, all day
• All the students passed the exam.
(Barcha talabalar imtihondan o'tdi.)

every day = har kuni · all day = kun bo'yi
everybody/everything + birlik fe'l: Everybody is here.

q.q: I go to the gym ___ day.
I was at home ___ day yesterday. I didn't go out.
q.uz: Kecha kun bo'yi uyda edim. Tashqariga chiqmadim.

intro:
Bu mavzuda every va all farqini o'rganamiz. Ikkalasi ham "hamma, har" degan ma'noni beradi:
• every + birlik ot: every day (har kuni), every student (har bir o'quvchi)
• all + ko'plik yoki sanalmaydigan: all students (barcha o'quvchilar), all day (kun bo'yi)
explain:
1. every va all

every + birlikall + ko'plik
Every student has a book.All (the) students have books.
every cityall cities
Ma'nosi bir xil, lekin every dan keyin birlik ot va birlik fe'l keladi.

2. every day va all day — farqi katta!

• every day = har kuni: I work every day. (Har kuni ishlayman.)
• all day = kun bo'yi: I worked all day. (Kun bo'yi ishladim.)
Xuddi shunday: every morning (har ertalab) / all morning (ertalab bo'yi).

3. everybody, everything, everywhere

• Everybody is happy. (Hamma xursand.) — birlik fe'l!
• I understood everything. (Hammasini tushundim.)
"All is…" emas, Everything is…

4. all + of

all my friends = all of my friends · all of them
tip: O'zbekchadagi "har" (har kuni, har bir) = every + birlik; "barcha, hamma" = all + ko'plik; "…bo'yi" (kun bo'yi) = all day.
ex: I go for a walk every evening.
All the shops are closed on Sunday.

title: all / most / some / any / no / none
lesson:
Umumiy: most people, some cars, no money
Aniq guruh: most of my friends, some of the cars, none of them

• Most people like music.
(Ko'pchilik musiqani yoqtiradi.)
• Most of my friends live in Tashkent.
(Do'stlarimning ko'pi Toshkentda yashaydi.)
• None of them came.
(Ulardan hech biri kelmadi.)

⚠️ most of the / most of my (not most of people)

q.w: my friends — aniq guruh → Most of.

q.q: I invited five friends, but ___ them came.
q.uz: Besh do'stimni taklif qildim, lekin hech biri kelmadi.
q.w: them haqida, hech biri → none of.

q.q: ___ of the students passed. Only two failed. (ko'pchilik)
q.uz: Talabalarning ko'pi o'tdi. Faqat ikkitasi yiqildi.

q.q: Some ___ the books are very old.
Did ___ of you see the film? (birortangiz)

intro:
Bu mavzuda miqdor bildiruvchi so'zlarni o'rganamiz: all (hamma), most (ko'pchilik), some (ba'zilari), any, no / none (hech biri).

Ular ikki xil ishlatiladi:
• Umuman: Most people like music. (Ko'pchilik odamlar musiqani yoqtiradi.)
• Aniq guruhdan (of bilan): Most of my friends live here. (Do'stlarimning ko'pi shu yerda yashaydi.)
explain:
1. Umuman — of siz

So'zMisolTarjima

someSome cars are electric.Ba'zi mashinalar elektr bilan yuradi.

2. Aniq guruh — of + the / my / these / them

So'zMisol

most ofmost of the students
some ofsome of these books
none ofnone of us

3. Eng ko'p xato

• "Most of people" ❌ → Most people (umuman) yoki most of the people (aniq) ✅
• "the most people" ❌ — bu boshqa ma'no (eng ko'p)
tip: O'zbekchada "odamlarning ko'pi" va "ko'p odamlar" deymiz. Inglizchada umuman bo'lsa most people, aniq guruh bo'lsa most of the / my ….
ex: Most people in Uzbekistan speak Russian.
Most of my colleagues are young.
Some of the questions were very difficult.
None of us knew the answer.
All of them came to the wedding.
Some people don't like cold weather.
mi: Most of my friends are students.

title: both / either / neither
lesson:
both — ikkalasi ham: Both restaurants are good.
(Ikkala restoran ham yaxshi.)
either — ikkalasidan biri, farqi yo'q: We can go to either restaurant.
(Istalgan biriga borishimiz mumkin.)
neither — ikkalasi ham emas: Neither restaurant is open.
(Ikkalasi ham ochiq emas.)

both … and · either … or · neither … nor

q.q: I have two brothers. ___ of them are students.
q.uz: Ikki akam bor. Ikkalasi ham talaba.

q.q: Tea or coffee? — ___ . I don't mind.
q.uz: Choymi yoki qahva? — Farqi yo'q, istalgan biri.

q.q: ___ of my parents speak English. They speak only Uzbek.

q.uz: U ham inglizcha, ham ruscha gapiradi.

q.q: You can have ___ tea or coffee.
___ Ali nor Tom came to the lesson.
q.uz: Ali ham, Tom ham darsga kelmadi.

q.q: There are two roads. You can take ___ road.
q.uz: Ikki yo'l bor. Istalganidan borishingiz mumkin.

intro:
Bu mavzuda ikki narsa yoki ikki odam haqida gapirganda ishlatiladigan so'zlarni o'rganamiz:
• both — ikkalasi ham: Both restaurants are good.
• either — ikkalasidan biri (farqi yo'q): You can take either road.
• neither — ikkalasi ham … emas: Neither answer is correct.
explain:
1. Ma'nolar

So'zMa'nosiMisol
bothikkalasi ham ✅✅Both my brothers are doctors.
eitheru yoki bu ✅/✅Tea or coffee? — Either. I don't mind.
neitherikkalasi ham emas ❌❌Neither of them came.

2. Juft bog'lovchilar

• both … and — ham …, ham …: She speaks both English and French.
• either … or — yo …, yo …: We can go either today or tomorrow.
• neither … nor — na …, na …: Neither Ali nor Vali was there.

3. of bilan

both of / either of / neither of + the / my / them / us:
Neither of my parents smokes. (Ota-onamning hech biri chekmaydi.)

4. Fe'l

both — ko'plik fe'l (Both are…); either / neither — odatda birlik fe'l (Neither is…).
tip: O'zbekchadagi "ikkalasi ham" = both; "istalgan biri" = either; "ikkalasi ham … emas / na …, na …" = neither (… nor).
ex: Both my sisters live in Tashkent.
You can sit on either side.
Neither of the hotels was cheap.
Ikkala mehmonxona ham arzon emas edi.
I like both tea and coffee.
Men ham choyni, ham qahvani yoqtiraman.
You can pay either by card or in cash.
Yo karta bilan, yo naqd pul bilan to'lashingiz mumkin.
Neither Ali nor his brother came.
mi: Either Ali and Vali can help.
Either Ali or Vali can help.

title: a lot / much / many
lesson:
many + sanaladigan ko'plik: many books, many people
much + sanalmaydigan: much money, much time
a lot of — ikkalasiga ham (ayniqsa ijobiy gapda)

• How many children have they got?
(Ularning nechta farzandi bor?)
• I don't have much time.
(Vaqtim ko'p emas.)
• She has a lot of friends.
(Uning do'stlari ko'p.)

q.q: There weren't ___ people at the party.
Did you take ___ photos on holiday?

intro:
Bu mavzuda "ko'p" ma'nosini bildiruvchi uch so'zni farqlaymiz:
• many + sanaladigan ko'plik: many books, many people
• much + sanalmaydigan: much money, much time
• a lot of — ikkalasiga ham: a lot of books, a lot of money
explain:
1. Jadval

Sanaladigan (books)Sanalmaydigan (money)
Ijobiy (+)a lot of booksa lot of money
Inkor (−)not many booksnot much money
Savol (?)How many books?How much money?

2. Qoida

• Ijobiy gaplarda odatda a lot of: I have a lot of friends.
• Inkor va savolda ko'pincha many / much: I don't have much time. Do you have many friends?
• "I have much money" — grammatik to'g'ri, lekin g'alati eshitiladi. Yaxshisi: I have a lot of money.

3. Otsiz

• Do you drink coffee? — Yes, a lot. (of siz!)
• Thank you very much.
tip: O'zbekchada "ko'p" har doim bir xil. Inglizchada otga qarang: sanash mumkin bo'lsa (kitob, odam) → many; sanab bo'lmasa (pul, vaqt, suv) → much; ishonch bo'lmasa → a lot of.
ex: How many brothers have you got?
I don't have much free time.
There were a lot of people at the market.
How much sugar do you want?
We have a lot of homework today.
mi: I like it a lot of.

title: (a) little / (a) few
lesson:
a little + sanalmaydigan: biroz (yetarli)
a few + ko'plik: bir nechta (yetarli)
• I have a little money. Let's go out.
(Biroz pulim bor. Tashqariga chiqaylik.)
• I have a few friends here.
(Bu yerda bir nechta do'stim bor.)

little / few (a siz): juda oz, deyarli yo'q
• He has few friends. He's lonely.
(Uning do'stlari juda oz. U yolg'iz.)

q.q: I have ___ money. Let's go out for dinner.
q.uz: Biroz pulim bor. Kechki ovqatga chiqaylik.
Bu yerda bir nechta do'stim bor.
q.w: friends — sanaladi, bir nechta → a few.

q.q: He has ___ friends. He's very lonely.
q.uz: Uning do'stlari juda oz. U juda yolg'iz.

q.q: Can I have a ___ milk in my tea?
I'll be ready in a ___ minutes.

q.w: Vaqt juda oz, shoshilish kerak → little.

q.q: We stayed in Samarkand for ___ days.

intro:
Bu mavzuda "oz" ma'nosini bildiruvchi so'zlarni o'rganamiz. Bu yerda bitta a harfi ma'noni butunlay o'zgartiradi:
• a little / a few — biroz, bir nechta (yetarli, ijobiy): I have a few friends here. 😊
• little / few — juda oz, deyarli yo'q (salbiy): He has few friends. 😟
explain:
1. Qaysi ot bilan?

SanalmaydiganSanaladigan ko'plik
Biroz (yetarli)a little moneya few friends
Juda oz (yetmaydi)little moneyfew friends

2. Ma'no farqi

• I have a little money. Let's go to the café. (Biroz pulim bor. Kafega boraylik.) — ijobiy
• I have little money. I can't buy it. (Pulim juda oz. Sotib ololmayman.) — salbiy

• She has a few friends. (Uning bir nechta do'sti bor.)
• She has few friends. She's lonely. (Do'stlari juda oz. U yolg'iz.)

3. Iboralar

• a little + sifat: I'm a little tired. (Biroz charchadim.)
• a few days / minutes: in a few minutes (bir necha daqiqadan keyin)
• I speak a little English. (Biroz inglizcha gapiraman.)
tip: O'zbekchadagi "biroz / bir nechta" = a little / a few. "Juda oz / deyarli yo'q" = little / few (a siz). Og'zaki nutqda ko'pincha a little / a few ishlatiladi.
ex: Can you wait a few minutes?
Add a little salt to the soup.
Few people know about this place.
Bu joy haqida juda kam odam biladi.

title: old / nice / interesting (adjectives)
lesson:
Sifat otdan oldin keladi va ko'plikda o'zgarmaydi:
• a nice day · nice days (not nices)
• an old house
(eski uy)

be/look/feel/smell/taste/sound + sifat:
• You look tired.
(Charchagan ko'rinasiz.)
• This soup tastes good.
(Bu sho'rva mazali.)

⚠️ a red big car ✗ → a big red car ✓ (o'lcham → rang)

q.q: It's a ___ day today. The sun is shining. (nice)
q.uz: Bugun yoqimli kun. Quyosh charaqlab turibdi.

intro:
Sifat (adjective) — narsa yoki odamning qanday ekanini bildiradi: big, nice, old, interesting.

Ingliz tilida sifat:
• otdan oldin keladi: a nice day (not a day nice)
• ko'plikda o'zgarmaydi: nice days (not nices)
• be, look, feel, taste dan keyin ham keladi: You look tired.
explain:
1. Joylashuvi

JoyiMisol
Ot oldidanan old house, beautiful flowers

look / feel / seem / sound / taste / smell dan keyinYou look happy. It tastes good.

2. Sifat o'zgarmaydi

• a big car → two big cars (not bigs)
• She is tall. They are tall.

3. Bir nechta sifat — tartib

Odatda: fikr → o'lcham → yosh → rang → material
• a nice big old house
• a small red car (not a red small car)
• a beautiful long black dress

4. look + sifat (ravish emas!)

• You look tired. (not tiredly)
• This soup tastes good. (not well)
tip: O'zbekchada ham sifat otdan oldin keladi (katta uy, chiroyli gul) — bu oson. Faqat esda tuting: inglizchada sifat ko'plikda o'zgarmaydi (big cars) va "ko'rinmoq" (look) dan keyin ham sifat keladi.
ex: We live in a small flat.

title: quickly / badly / suddenly (adverbs)
lesson:
Ravish ish-harakat qanday bajarilishini bildiradi: sifat + -ly
quick → quickly · slow → slowly · careful → carefully · easy → easily

• He drives carefully.
(U ehtiyotkorlik bilan haydaydi.)
• She speaks English very well.
(U inglizchada juda yaxshi gapiradi.)

⚠️ good → well · fast → fast · hard → hard · late → late

q.q: She works very ___ . She's never tired. (hard)
q.uz: U juda qattiq ishlaydi. Hech charchamaydi.

Ravish (adverb) — ish-harakat qanday bajarilishini bildiradi. U ko'pincha sifatga -ly qo'shib yasaladi:
quick → quickly (tez) · slow → slowly (sekin) · careful → carefully (ehtiyotkorlik bilan)

• Sifat — otni tasvirlaydi: He's a careful driver.
• Ravish — fe'lni tasvirlaydi: He drives carefully.
explain:
1. Yasalishi

3. Sifatmi yoki ravish?

• She is a good singer. (ot oldida → sifat)
• She sings well. (fe'ldan keyin → ravish)
• Please speak slowly. (Iltimos, sekin gapiring.)
⚠️ "She speaks English very good" — xato. To'g'risi: very well.
tip: O'zbekchada sifat va ravish ko'pincha bir xil: "yaxshi odam" va "yaxshi gapiradi". Inglizchada esa farq bor: a good man, but he speaks well.
ex: The children played happily in the garden.

title: old / older · expensive / more expensive
lesson:
Qisqa sifat + -er: old → older, cheap → cheaper, big → bigger, easy → easier
Uzun sifat: more + sifat: more expensive, more interesting

Noto'g'ri: good → better · bad → worse · far → further/farther

• My brother is older than me.
(Akam mendan katta.)
• This book is more interesting.
(Bu kitob qiziqroq.)

q.q: This book is ___ than that one.
Moscow is ___ than Tashkent in winter.
The weather today is ___ than yesterday.

intro:
Qiyosiy daraja (comparative) — ikki narsani solishtirish uchun: kattaroq, arzonroq, qiziqroq.

• Qisqa sifat + -er: old → older, cheap → cheaper
• Uzun sifat: more + sifat: more expensive, more interesting

O'zbek tilida bunga "-roq" qo'shimchasi to'g'ri keladi: kattaroq, arzonroq.

3. Ikki usulni aralashtirmang!

"more bigger" ❌ → bigger ✅ · "more better" ❌ → better ✅
tip: O'zbekchadagi "-roq" (kattaroq, yaxshiroq) inglizchada -er yoki more bo'ladi. Qisqa so'z bo'lsa -er, uzun so'z bo'lsa more.
ex: My brother is taller than me.

title: older than ... · more expensive than ...
lesson:
• My brother is older than me.
(Akam mendan katta.)
• Trains are faster than buses.
(Poyezdlar avtobuslardan tezroq.)

Farqni kuchaytirish: much / a lot / a bit + comparative
• Your car is much bigger than mine.
(Mashinangiz menikidan ancha katta.)
• It's a bit cheaper.
(Biroz arzonroq.)

q.q: Your car is ___ bigger than mine.
This phone is ___ expensive than that one.
She's a ___ taller than her sister. (biroz)
I'm ___ at maths than my brother.
This exam was ___ than the last one.

intro:
Bu mavzuda solishtirishda than (… dan) so'zini ishlatishni o'rganamiz:
My brother is older than me. (Akam mendan katta.)

Farqni kuchaytirish uchun: much / a lot (ancha) yoki a bit / a little (biroz):
Your car is much bigger than mine. (Mashinangiz menikidan ancha katta.)
explain:
1. Shakli

qiyosiy sifat + than + kim/nima
MisolTarjima

Trains are faster than buses.Poyezdlar avtobuslardan tezroq.

2. than dan keyin olmosh

• He's older than me. (og'zaki) = He's older than I am.

3. Farq darajasi

So'zMa'nosiMisol
much / a lot / farancha, judamuch cheaper

⚠️ "very bigger" ❌ → much bigger ✅
tip: O'zbekchadagi "-dan" (mendan katta, avtobusdan tez) = than. "Ancha" = much, "biroz" = a bit. "Very" qiyosiy daraja bilan ishlatilmaydi!
ex: This book is much more interesting than that one.
She's a little older than her husband.

title: not as ... as
lesson:
as + sifat + as — teng: Ali is as tall as Tom.
(Ali Tom bilan bir xil bo'yda.)
not as … as — kamroq: Bukhara isn't as big as Tashkent.
(Buxoro Toshkentchalik katta emas.)

• I'm not as old as you.
(Men sizchalik katta emasman.)
the same as: Your phone is the same as mine.
(Telefoningiz menikiga o'xshash/bir xil.)

q.uz: Ali Tom bilan bir xil bo'yda.

q.q: Your phone is the same ___ mine.
The film wasn't ___ good as the book.
He's not as ___ as his brother.
My English is not as good ___ yours.

intro:
Bu mavzuda teng yoki teng emasligini bildirishni o'rganamiz:
• as … as — …dek, …chalik (teng): Ali is as tall as Vali. (Ali Valichalik baland.)
• not as … as — …chalik emas: Bukhara isn't as big as Tashkent. (Buxoro Toshkentchalik katta emas.)
explain:
1. Shakli

as + sifat (oddiy shakl!) + as
GapMa'nosi
Ali is as tall as Vali.Bo'ylari teng.
Ali isn't as tall as Vali.Vali balandroq.
Run as fast as you can!Imkoni boricha tez yuguring!
⚠️ as … as orasida sifat oddiy shaklda: as big as (not as bigger as).

2. not as … as = qiyosiy daraja

• Bukhara isn't as big as Tashkent. = Tashkent is bigger than Bukhara.

3. the same as

• Your phone is the same as mine. (Telefoningiz menikiga o'xshash.)
• the same + ot + as: She is the same age as me. (U men bilan tengdosh.)
tip: O'zbekchadagi "-chalik / -dek" (sizchalik, otasidek) = as … as. "-chalik emas" = not as … as.
ex: My son is as tall as me now.
The film wasn't as good as the book.
This car isn't as expensive as that one.
She's the same age as my sister.
I can't run as fast as you.
mi: He isn't so tall like me.
He isn't as tall as me.

title: the oldest · the most expensive
lesson:
Qisqa sifat: the + -est: old → the oldest, big → the biggest, easy → the easiest
Uzun sifat: the most + sifat: the most expensive
Noto'g'ri: good → the best · bad → the worst

• Everest is the highest mountain in the world.
(Everest dunyodagi eng baland tog'.)
• It's the best film I've ever seen.
(Bu men ko'rgan eng yaxshi film.)

q.q: Everest is ___ mountain in the world.
It's the ___ film I've ever seen. (good)
q.uz: Bu men ko'rgan eng yaxshi film.

q.q: This is ___ hotel in the city.
Ali is the ___ student in our class.
What's the ___ river in the world?

intro:
Orttirma daraja (superlative) — guruhdagi eng katta, eng yaxshi narsani bildiradi.

• Qisqa sifat: the + -est: the oldest, the cheapest
• Uzun sifat: the most + sifat: the most expensive

Everest is the highest mountain in the world. (Everest — dunyodagi eng baland tog'.)
explain:
1. Qoidalar

SifatQiyosiyOrttirma
oldolderthe oldest
bigbiggerthe biggest
easyeasierthe easiest
expensivemore expensivethe most expensive
goodbetterthe best
badworsethe worst

2. Qanday ishlatiladi

• Doim the bilan: the best (not best)
• Joy uchun in: the biggest city in Uzbekistan
• Guruh uchun of: the youngest of the three brothers
• Present perfect + ever: It's the best film I've ever seen.
tip: O'zbekchadagi "eng" (eng katta, eng yaxshi) = the …est yoki the most …. "Dunyodagi" = in the world.
ex: Tashkent is the biggest city in Central Asia.
Toshkent Markaziy Osiyodagi eng katta shahar.
This is the most beautiful place I've ever seen.
Bu men ko'rgan eng go'zal joy.
Who is the oldest person in your family?
It was the worst day of my life.
Bu hayotimdagi eng yomon kun edi.
She's the best student in the class.
What's the cheapest way to get there?
U yerga borishning eng arzon yo'li qaysi?

title: enough
lesson:
enough + ot: enough money, enough time
• I don't have enough money.
(Pulim yetarli emas.)

sifat + enough: old enough, big enough
• He isn't old enough to drive.
(U mashina haydashga hali yosh.)

• Is the room warm enough for you?
(Xona sizga yetarlicha issiqmi?)

q.q: This bag isn't big ___ for all my things.
q.uz: Bu sumka barcha narsalarimga yetarlicha katta emas.

intro:
Enough — yetarli, yetarlicha. Uning joyi muhim:
• enough + ot: I don't have enough money. (Pulim yetarli emas.)
• sifat + enough: He isn't old enough. (U yetarlicha katta emas.)
explain:
1. Joylashuvi

TuzilishMisolTarjima
enough + otenough time, enough chairsyetarli vaqt, yetarli stul
sifat + enoughbig enough, warm enoughyetarlicha katta / issiq
ravish + enoughfast enoughyetarlicha tez
⚠️ Sifat bilan enough keyin keladi: old enough (not enough old).

2. + to + fe'l

• She's old enough to drive. (U mashina haydash uchun yetarlicha katta.)
• We don't have enough time to finish. (Tugatish uchun vaqtimiz yetmaydi.)

3. + for + kishi

• This bag isn't big enough for me.
• Is there enough food for everybody? (Hammaga ovqat yetadimi?)

4. Otsiz

• Have you got money? — Not enough. · I've had enough. (Yetadi, to'ydim.)
tip: O'zbekchadagi "yetarli / yetmaydi" = enough / not enough. Faqat sifat bilan tartibga e'tibor bering: "yetarlicha issiq" = warm enough (so'zma-so'z: issiq yetarlicha).
ex: There aren't enough chairs for everyone.
Is the water warm enough to swim?
I didn't sleep enough last night.
He's not tall enough to play basketball.
U basketbol o'ynash uchun yetarlicha baland emas.
mi: She is enough clever for this job.
She is clever enough for this job.

title: too
lesson:
too + sifat = haddan tashqari, juda (salbiy):
• This coffee is too hot. I can't drink it.
(Bu qahva juda issiq. Icholmayman.)

too much + sanalmaydigan · too many + ko'plik
• There's too much traffic.
(Tirbandlik haddan ziyod.)
• There are too many people here.
(Bu yerda odam juda ko'p.)

too … to: It's too cold to swim.
(Suzish uchun juda sovuq.)

q.q: This coffee is ___ . I can't drink it.
There are ___ people here. Let's go.
q.uz: Bu yerda odam juda ko'p. Ketaylik.

q.q: He's ___ young to watch this film.
q.uz: U bu filmni ko'rish uchun juda yosh.

q.q: I ate too ___ cake. Now I feel sick.
q.uz: Juda ko'p tort yedim. Endi ko'nglim aynayapti.
q.w: cake — bu yerda sanalmaydi → too much.

q.q: These shoes are ___ . I need a bigger size.
q.uz: Bu tuflilar juda kichik. Kattaroq o'lcham kerak.

q.q: You make too ___ mistakes. Be careful.
q.uz: Juda ko'p xato qilyapsiz. Ehtiyot bo'ling.

intro:
Too — haddan tashqari, juda (salbiy ma'noda, ya'ni muammo bor):
This coffee is too hot. I can't drink it. (Bu qahva haddan tashqari issiq. Icholmayman.)

• too much + sanalmaydigan: too much sugar
• too many + sanaladigan: too many people
explain:
1. Shakllar

TuzilishMisol
too + sifattoo big, too expensive
too much + sanalmaydigantoo much noise, too much work
too many + sanaladigan ko'pliktoo many cars, too many mistakes
fe'l + too muchYou talk too much.

2. too va very farqi

• It's very hot, but I can drink it. — juda issiq, lekin muammo yo'q.
• It's too hot. I can't drink it. — haddan tashqari, muammo bor.

3. too … to + fe'l

• He's too young to drive. (U mashina haydash uchun juda yosh.)
• It's too cold to go out. (Tashqariga chiqish uchun juda sovuq.)

4. too va enough

too big = not small enough · too young = not old enough
tip: O'zbekchada "juda" ikki ma'noda ishlatiladi. Inglizchada farq bor: shunchaki "juda" → very; "haddan tashqari, shuning uchun bo'lmaydi" → too.
ex: These jeans are too small for me.
There's too much salt in the soup.
There are too many people here.
Bu yerda odam haddan tashqari ko'p.
It's too late to call him now.
Hozir unga qo'ng'iroq qilish uchun juda kech.
You work too much. You need a rest.
Siz juda ko'p ishlaysiz. Dam olishingiz kerak.
This phone is too expensive for me.
Bu telefon men uchun juda qimmat.

title: He speaks English very well. (word order 1)
lesson:
Fe'l va to'ldiruvchi orasiga boshqa so'z qo'yilmaydi:
• He speaks English very well. (not speaks very well English)
(U inglizchada juda yaxshi gapiradi.)
• I like music very much. (not like very much music)
(Musiqani juda yoqtiraman.)

Joy + vaqt tartibi: where → when
• I went to the bank yesterday.
(Kecha bankka bordim.)

q.uz: U har kuni ertalab qahva ichadi.
Biz ishga soat 8 da yetib keldik.
Ular uch yildan beri Londonda yashashadi.
o: have lived in London for three years
have lived for three years in London in
in London have lived for three years

intro:
Ingliz tilida so'z tartibi qat'iy. Eng muhim qoida: fe'l va to'ldiruvchi orasiga boshqa so'z qo'yilmaydi.

✅ He speaks English very well.
❌ He speaks very well English.

Joy va vaqt kelsa: avval joy, keyin vaqt: I went to the bank yesterday.
explain:
1. Asosiy tartib

EgaFe'lTo'ldiruvchiQandayQayerdaQachon
Ireadthe bookquicklyat homeyesterday

2. Fe'l + to'ldiruvchi — ajratilmaydi

• I like music very much. (not I like very much music)
• She cleaned the room carefully. (not cleaned carefully the room)
• Did you find your keys?

3. Joy → vaqt

• We arrived at the hotel at 8.
• She has lived in London for ten years.
• I'm going to Samarkand tomorrow.

4. Vaqt gap boshida ham bo'lishi mumkin

Yesterday I went to the bank. ✅
tip: O'zbekchada fe'l oxirida keladi: "Men kecha bankka bordim". Inglizchada esa fe'l egadan keyin darhol keladi va tartib teskari: I went to the bank yesterday (joy → vaqt).
ex: I like Uzbek food very much.
We met our teacher in the park yesterday.
He drives his car very fast.
I'll see you at the station at 6.
They have lived in Bukhara since 2010.
mi: I went yesterday to the bank.
I went to the bank yesterday.

title: always / usually / often (word order 2)
lesson:
always · usually · often · sometimes · rarely · never — asosiy fe'ldan oldin:
• I always get up early.
(Men doim erta turaman.)

Lekin be dan keyin:
• She is always late.
(U doim kechikadi.)

Yordamchi fe'ldan keyin: I have never been there. · I can never remember.

q.uz: Men u yerda hech qachon bo'lmaganman.

q.q: We ___ to the cinema on Sundays.
q.uz: Biz odatda yakshanba kunlari kinoga boramiz.
U ishdan keyin ko'pincha charchagan bo'ladi.

intro:
Bu mavzuda takrorlanishni bildiruvchi so'zlarning gapdagi o'rnini o'rganamiz: always (doim), usually (odatda), often (tez-tez), sometimes (ba'zan), rarely (kamdan-kam), never (hech qachon).

• Oddiy fe'ldan oldin: I always get up early.
• be fe'lidan keyin: She is always late.
explain:
1. Ishonch darajasi

always 100% → usually 90% → often 70% → sometimes 50% → rarely / seldom 10% → never 0%

2. Joylashuvi

HolatJoyiMisol
Oddiy fe'lfe'ldan oldinI often read.
be (am/is/are/was)be dan keyinHe is never late.
Yordamchi fe'l (can, have, will)yordamchidan keyinI have never been there.
Inkornot dan keyinI don't usually eat meat.

3. sometimes — erkinroq

Sometimes I walk to work. / I sometimes walk to work. — ikkalasi ham to'g'ri.

4. never — o'zi inkor

I never smoke. ✅ · I don't never smoke. ❌
tip: O'zbekchada "doim", "odatda" so'zlari ko'pincha gap boshida keladi. Inglizchada esa ular gap o'rtasida, fe'lning yonida turadi: I always drink tea.
ex: We often go to the mountains.
I have never seen snow in summer.
mi: I go always to school by bus.
I always go to school by bus.

title: still / yet / already
lesson:
still = hali ham (davom etyapti): It's still raining.
(Hali ham yomg'ir yog'yapti.)
yet = hali (inkor/savol, gap oxirida): He hasn't come yet.
(U hali kelmadi.)
already = allaqachon (kutilganidan oldin): I've already eaten.
(Allaqachon ovqatlandim.)

• Do you still live in Tashkent?
(Hali ham Toshkentda yashaysizmi?)

q.uz: Hali ham yomg'ir yog'yapti. Soyabon oling.

q.q: Do you ___ live in Tashkent? (hali ham)
It's only 9 o'clock and she's ___ gone to bed.
q.uz: Soat endi 9 bo'ldi, u esa allaqachon yotib qoldi.

q.q: I ___ don't understand. Can you explain again?

intro:
Bu mavzuda uchta muhim so'zni farqlaymiz:
• still — hali ham (davom etyapti): It's still raining.
• yet — hali (kutilyapti, inkor/savolda): He hasn't come yet.
• already — allaqachon (kutilganidan oldin): I've already eaten.
explain:
1. Ma'nolari

So'zMa'nosiMisol
stillhali ham davom etyapti, tugamadiDo you still live in Tashkent?
yethali bo'lmadi (−) / bo'ldimi? (?)Has the bus come yet?
alreadyallaqachon bo'ldi (kutilmaganda erta)She's already left.

2. Joylashuvi

• still — fe'ldan oldin, be dan keyin: I still remember. · She is still here.
• yet — gap oxirida: I haven't finished yet.
• already — fe'ldan oldin yoki have dan keyin: I've already paid.

3. still not va not yet

• I still haven't found a job. — kutish uzoq davom etyapti (norozilik)
• I haven't found a job yet. — hali topmadim (oddiy)
tip: O'zbekchada: "hali ham" = still, "hali …-madi" = not … yet, "allaqachon" = already. Unit 16 dagi just / already / yet ni ham eslang.
ex: He's 30, but he still lives with his parents.
U 30 yoshda, lekin hali ham ota-onasi bilan yashaydi.

title: Give me that book! Give it to me!
lesson:
give/send/show/lend/buy + kishi + narsa:
• Give me the book.
(Kitobni menga bering.)
narsa + to/for + kishi:
• Give the book to me.

Narsa it/them bo'lsa, faqat ikkinchi shakl:
• Give it to me. (not Give me it)
(Uni menga bering.)
• I bought a present for my mother.
(Onamga sovg'a sotib oldim.)

q.q: I sent a letter ___ my friend.
I bought a present ___ my mother.
These are Tom's keys. Can you give ___ ?
q.uz: Bular Tomning kalitlari. Ularni unga bera olasizmi?

intro:
Bu mavzuda give, send, show, lend, buy kabi fe'llardan keyin ikki to'ldiruvchi (kishi va narsa) qanday tartibda kelishini o'rganamiz:
• fe'l + kishi + narsa: Give me the book.
• fe'l + narsa + to/for + kishi: Give the book to me.

Ikkalasi ham to'g'ri. Lekin narsa it / them bo'lsa, faqat ikkinchisi: Give it to me.
explain:
1. Ikki tartib

Kishi + narsaNarsa + to/for + kishi
I gave Ali a present.I gave a present to Ali.
Show me your photos.Show your photos to me.
She bought her mother flowers.She bought flowers for her mother.

2. to yoki for?

• to: give, send, show, lend, sell, pass, tell — narsa kishiga boradi
• for: buy, make, get, cook — kishi uchun qilinadi

3. it / them bo'lsa

• Give it to me. ✅ — Give me it. ❌
• Send them to her. ✅ — Send her them. ❌
tip: O'zbekchada "menga kitobni ber" yoki "kitobni menga ber" — ikkalasi ham bo'ladi. Inglizchada ham ikki tartib bor, faqat "-ga" ni to, "uchun" ni for bilan bering.
ex: Can you pass me the salt?
I sent an email to my teacher.
He bought his wife a ring.
This is my book. Give it to me!
Bu mening kitobim. Uni menga bering!
My grandmother made a cake for us.
mi: I sent to him a letter.
She bought a dress to me.
She bought a dress for me.

title: at 8 o'clock · on Monday · in April
lesson:
at + soat: at 8 o'clock, at noon, at night, at the weekend
on + kun/sana: on Monday, on 5 May, on my birthday
in + oy/yil/fasl/kun qismi: in April, in 2025, in summer, in the morning

• The lesson starts at 9.
(Dars soat 9 da boshlanadi.)
• I was born in 1995.
(Men 1995 yilda tug'ilganman.)

⚠️ next/last/this/every oldidan predlog yo'q: next week, last Monday

Take off your shoes. / Take your shoes off.Take them off.
tip: O'zbekchada "chiroqni o'chir" deymiz va "o'chirmoq" bitta fe'l. Inglizchada esa ikki qismli: turn off. "Uni o'chir" = turn it off (it doim o'rtada).
ex: Put on your jacket. It's cold.
Can I try these shoes on?
This is my book. Give it back!

title: and / but / or / so / because
lesson:
and — va · but — lekin · or — yoki
so — shuning uchun (natija) · because — chunki (sabab)

• I was tired, so I went to bed.
(Charchagan edim, shuning uchun yotdim.)
• I went to bed because I was tired.
(Yotdim, chunki charchagan edim.)
• It's cheap but very good.
(U arzon, lekin juda yaxshi.)

q.q: I was tired, ___ I went to bed.
I went to bed ___ I was tired.
It was raining, ___ we didn't go out.
q.uz: Yomg'ir yog'ayotgan edi, shuning uchun tashqariga chiqmadik.

q.q: She's learning English ___ she wants to work abroad.
q.uz: U ingliz tilini o'rganyapti, chunki chet elda ishlamoqchi.

intro:
Bog'lovchilar gaplarni bir-biriga bog'laydi:
• and — va · but — lekin · or — yoki
• so — shuning uchun (natija) · because — chunki (sabab)

I was tired, so I went to bed. = I went to bed because I was tired.
explain:
1. Jadval

So'zMa'nosiMisol
andva, hamdaI bought bread and milk.
butlekin, ammoIt's cheap but good.
oryokiTea or coffee?
soshuning uchun (natija)It was late, so I took a taxi.
becausechunki (sabab)I took a taxi because it was late.

2. so va because — eng ko'p adashtiriladi

• Sabab → so → natija: It was raining, so we stayed at home.
• Natija → because → sabab: We stayed at home because it was raining.

3. Inkor gapda or

I don't like tea or coffee. (Na choyni, na qahvani yoqtiraman.)
tip: O'zbekchada: "…ganligi uchun / chunki" = because (sabab), "shuning uchun" = so (natija). Avval nima bo'lganiga qarang: sabab birinchi kelsa — so.
ex: I called you, but you didn't answer.
Sizga qo'ng'iroq qildim, lekin javob bermadingiz.
Do you want to go out or stay at home?
The shop was closed, so we went home.
Do'kon yopiq edi, shuning uchun uyga ketdik.
She's happy because she passed the exam.
We had dinner and watched a film.
I was hungry, so I made a sandwich.
Och edim, shuning uchun buterbrod qildim.
mi: I was tired, because I went to bed.
I was tired, so I went to bed.
I stayed home so I was ill.
I stayed home because I was ill.
I don't like tea and coffee.
I don't like tea or coffee.
It was cold, because I wore a coat.
It was cold, so I wore a coat.

title: When ...
lesson:
Kelajak haqida gapirganda when / before / after / until / as soon as dan keyin present simple ishlatiladi (will emas):

• When I get home, I'll call you.
(Uyga yetib borganimda sizga qo'ng'iroq qilaman.)
• Wait here until I come back.
(Men qaytgunimcha shu yerda kuting.)

⚠️ When I get home … (not When I will get home)

q.q: When I ___ home, I'll call you.
q.uz: Uyga yetib borganimda sizga qo'ng'iroq qilaman.

q.q: I'll tell him when I ___ him tomorrow.
When I ___ young, I lived in Khiva. (be — past)
I'll call you as soon as I ___ the results. (get)
q.uz: Natijalarni olishim bilan sizga qo'ng'iroq qilaman.

q.q: What will you do when you ___ university?

intro:
Bu mavzuda muhim qoidani o'rganamiz: when, before, after, until, as soon as dan keyin kelajak haqida gapirganda will ishlatilmaydi, o'rniga hozirgi zamon (present simple) keladi.

When I get home, I'll call you. (Uyga yetib borganimda sizga qo'ng'iroq qilaman.)
❌ When I will get home…
explain:
1. Qoida

when / before / after / until / as soon as + PRESENTasosiy gap + WILL
When I finish work,I'll go home.
Before you leave,close the windows.
As soon as she arrives,we'll start.
Wait here until I come back.

2. Gap tartibi

Ikkala tartib ham to'g'ri:
• When I see him, I'll tell him.
• I'll tell him when I see him.
Gap when bilan boshlansa, o'rtasiga vergul qo'yiladi.

3. O'tgan zamonda

When I was a child, I lived in Khiva. (Bolaligimda Xivada yashardim.)
tip: O'zbekchada: "Uyga borganimda qo'ng'iroq qilaman" — birinchi qismda kelajak qo'shimchasi yo'q. Inglizchada ham xuddi shunday: When I get home (will yo'q), I'll call.
ex: When I finish university, I'll look for a job.
Call me as soon as you arrive.
Yetib borishingiz bilan menga qo'ng'iroq qiling.
Don't go out until the rain stops.
I'll make tea before the guests come.
When I was young, I played football every day.
After we eat, we'll go for a walk.
mi: When I will see him, I'll tell him.
When I see him, I'll tell him.
I'll wait until you will come.
Before you will go, call me.
As soon as I will know, I'll tell you.
As soon as I know, I'll tell you.

title: If we go ... If you see ...
lesson:
Bo'lishi mumkin bo'lgan holat:
If + present simple, … will + verb

• If it rains, we'll stay at home.
(Agar yomg'ir yog'sa, uyda qolamiz.)
• If you see Ali, tell him to call me.
(Alini ko'rsangiz, menga qo'ng'iroq qilsin deng.)

⚠️ If it rains … (not If it will rain)

q.q: If it ___ , we'll stay at home.
If you ___ Ali, tell him to call me.
q.uz: Alini ko'rsangiz, menga qo'ng'iroq qilsin deng.

q.q: If you study hard, you ___ pass the exam.
If I ___ time tomorrow, I'll visit you.
q.uz: Ertaga vaqtim bo'lsa, sizni ko'rgani boraman.

q.q: What will you do if you ___ the job?
q.uz: Agar ishga qabul qilinmasangiz nima qilasiz?

q.q: If you're hungry, I ___ make you a sandwich.
q.uz: Och bo'lsangiz, sizga buterbrod qilib beraman.

q.q: We'll miss the bus if we ___ hurry.
If she ___ late, we'll start without her. (be)

intro:
If — agar. Bu mavzuda haqiqatda bo'lishi mumkin bo'lgan shartlarni o'rganamiz (1-tur shart gap):

If it rains, we'll stay at home. (Agar yomg'ir yog'sa, uyda qolamiz.)

Qoida: if qismida hozirgi zamon, asosiy qismda will.
explain:
1. Shakli

If + present simplewill + fe'l
If you study,you'll pass the exam.
If it is sunny,we'll go to the park.
If I don't hurry,I'll miss the bus.
⚠️ If qismida will yo'q: If it rains (not If it will rain).

2. Boshqa shakllar

• If + present, buyruq: If you see Ali, tell him to call me.
• If + present, can / might: If you're free, we can go out.

3. when va if farqi

• When I see him… — albatta ko'raman.
• If I see him… — ko'rishim aniq emas.
tip: O'zbekchadagi "agar …-sa" (agar yog'sa, agar o'qisang) = If + present simple. Asosiy qism kelajakda bo'lsa → will.
ex: If you're hungry, I'll make you something.
Och bo'lsangiz, sizga biror narsa tayyorlayman.
If it's cold tomorrow, I won't go out.
If you see Lola, say hello from me.
If we leave now, we'll catch the train.
What will you do if you don't pass?
If I have time, I'll call you.
mi: If it will rain, we'll stay home.
If it rains, we'll stay home.
If I will see him, I'll tell him.
If I see him, I'll tell him.
If she don't come, we'll start.
If she doesn't come, we'll start.

title: If I had ... If we went ...
lesson:
Hozirgi/kelajakdagi xayoliy holat:
If + past simple, … would + verb

• If I had a lot of money, I would buy a house.
(Agar pulim ko'p bo'lsa edi, uy sotib olardim.)
• If I were you, I would go.
(Sizning o'rningizda bo'lsam, borardim.)

If I were (was ham mumkin) · would → 'd

q.q: If I ___ a lot of money, I would buy a house.
q.uz: Agar pulim ko'p bo'lsa edi, uy sotib olardim.

q.q: If I were you, I ___ go to the doctor.
If I ___ you, I'd take the job. (be)
q.w: If I were you (was ham mumkin).

q.q: What would you do if you ___ the lottery?
If I knew the answer, I ___ tell you.
If she ___ here, she would help us.
q.uz: U bu yerda bo'lsa edi, bizga yordam berardi.

q.q: I'd go out if it ___ so cold.
q.uz: Bunchalik sovuq bo'lmasa edi, tashqariga chiqardim.

q.q: If we ___ a car, we would drive to Samarkand. (have)
q.uz: Mashinamiz bo'lsa edi, Samarqandga mashinada borardik.

intro:
Bu mavzuda xayoliy, haqiqatga to'g'ri kelmaydigan shartlarni o'rganamiz (2-tur shart gap):

If I had a lot of money, I would buy a house. (Agar pulim ko'p bo'lsa edi, uy sotib olardim.) — lekin aslida pulim ko'p emas.

Qoida: if + o'tgan zamon, would + fe'l.
explain:
1. Shakli

If + past simplewould + fe'l
If I had a car,I would drive to work.
If she knew the answer,she'd tell you.
If I were you,I wouldn't go.
O'tgan zamon shakli ishlatiladi, lekin ma'no hozir yoki kelajak haqida (xayol).

2. If I were you

Maslahat berishning juda ko'p ishlatiladigan usuli:
If I were you, I would see a doctor. (Sizning o'rningizda bo'lsam, shifokorga borardim.)
I / he / she bilan ham were ishlatish mumkin (was ham og'zaki nutqda bo'ladi).

3. 1-tur va 2-tur shartni solishtiring

• If I have time, I'll help you. — bo'lishi mumkin (real).
• If I had time, I'd help you. — aslida vaqtim yo'q (xayol).
tip: O'zbekchadagi "agar …-sa edi, …-ar edim" (bo'lsa edi, olar edim) = If + past, would + fe'l. "Sizning o'rningizda bo'lsam" = If I were you.
ex: If I won the lottery, I would travel the world.
Lotereya yutsam, dunyo bo'ylab sayohat qilardim.
If I were you, I'd take the job.
If we lived near the sea, we'd swim every day.
Dengiz yaqinida yashasak edi, har kuni suzardik.
What would you do if you saw a ghost?
If she had more time, she would learn French.
Vaqti ko'proq bo'lsa edi, fransuz tilini o'rganardi.
I wouldn't do that if I were you.
mi: If I have money, I would buy it.
If I had money, I would buy it.
If I were you, I will go.
If I were you, I would go.
If he knows, he would tell.
If he knew, he would tell.

title: a person who ... a thing that/which ... (relative clauses 1)
lesson:
who — odamlar uchun · which — narsalar uchun · that — ikkalasi uchun

• A doctor is a person who helps sick people.
(Shifokor — kasallarga yordam beradigan odam.)
• This is the bus which goes to the airport.
(Bu aeroportga boradigan avtobus.)
• The man that lives next door is a teacher.
(Qo'shnimiz bo'lgan odam o'qituvchi.)

q.q: A doctor is a person ___ helps sick people.
This is the bus ___ goes to the airport.
The man ___ lives next door is a teacher. (odam)
I have a friend ___ speaks five languages.
Where's the book ___ was on the table?
A fridge is a machine ___ keeps food cold. (narsa)
The woman ___ called you is my sister.
q.uz: Sizga qo'ng'iroq qilgan ayol mening opam.

q.q: I lost the phone ___ my father gave me.

intro:
Nisbiy olmoshlar — ikki gapni bog'lab, odam yoki narsani aniqlashtiradi:
• who — odamlar uchun: a person who helps…
• which — narsalar uchun: the bus which goes…
• that — ikkalasi uchun ham

A doctor is a person who helps sick people. (Shifokor — kasallarga yordam beradigan odam.)
explain:
1. Jadval

Kim/nima uchunSo'zMisol
Odamwho / thatthe man who lives next door
Narsa, hayvonwhich / thatthe car which was stolen

2. Ikki gapni bog'lash

• I met a woman. She speaks five languages.
→ I met a woman who speaks five languages.
• This is the phone. It cost $1000.
→ This is the phone which / that cost $1000.

3. Diqqat

who/which olmosh o'rnini egallaydi, shuning uchun olmosh takrorlanmaydi:
❌ the man who he lives here → ✅ the man who lives here

4. what ishlatilmaydi

❌ the book what I bought → ✅ the book that / which I bought
tip: O'zbekchadagi "-gan / -digan" qo'shimchasi (yordam beradigan odam, o'g'irlangan mashina) inglizchada who / which / that bilan ifodalanadi. Faqat tartib teskari: odam who yordam beradi.
ex: I have a friend who lives in London.
This is the book which I told you about.
The woman who called you is my aunt.
Sizga qo'ng'iroq qilgan ayol mening xolam.
Where's the cake that was on the table?
A teacher is someone who teaches.
I like films that make me laugh.

title: the people we met · the hotel you stayed at (relative clauses 2)
lesson:
Agar who/which/that to'ldiruvchi bo'lsa, uni tushirib qoldirish mumkin:
• The people (who) we met were very nice.
(Biz uchrashgan odamlar juda yoqimli edi.)
• Did you like the film (that) we watched?
(Biz ko'rgan film yoqdimi?)

Predlog oxirida qoladi:
• The hotel we stayed at was cheap.
(Biz to'xtagan mehmonxona arzon edi.)

where — joy uchun: the town where I was born

q.uz: Biz uchrashgan odamlar juda yoqimli edi.

q.q: The hotel we stayed ___ was cheap.
This is the town ___ I was born.
The man I was talking ___ is my boss.

q.w: look for → for oxirida, olmosh yo'q.

q.q: The music we listened ___ was great.
The restaurant ___ we had dinner was expensive.
q.uz: Biz kechki ovqat qilgan restoran qimmat edi.

intro:
Bu mavzuda nisbiy gaplarning yana ikki xususiyatini o'rganamiz:
1) who/which/that to'ldiruvchi bo'lsa, uni tushirib qoldirish mumkin:
The people (who) we met were nice. (Biz uchrashgan odamlar yoqimli edi.)
2) Predlog gapning oxirida qoladi: the hotel we stayed at.
explain:
1. Qachon tushirib qoldirish mumkin?

who/which — ega (tushmaydi)who/which — to'ldiruvchi (tushishi mumkin)
the man who called methe man (who) I called
the bus which goes to the airportthe film (which) we watched
Oddiy test: who/which dan keyin yangi ega (I, we, you, she…) kelsa, uni tushirish mumkin.

2. Predlog oxirida

• the hotel we stayed at (biz to'xtagan mehmonxona)
• the man I was talking to (men gaplashayotgan odam)
• the music we listened to

3. where — joylar uchun

• the town where I was born (men tug'ilgan shahar)
• the restaurant where we had dinner

4. Olmosh takrorlanmaydi

❌ the film we watched it → ✅ the film we watched
tip: O'zbekchada "biz uchrashgan odamlar", "men tug'ilgan shahar" — bog'lovchi so'z yo'q. Inglizchada ham to'ldiruvchi bo'lsa who/which tushib qolishi mumkin: the people we met. Joy uchun where.
ex: The cake you made was delicious.
Is this the bag you were looking for?
The friends I met in Samarkand were very kind.
Samarqandda tanishgan do'stlarim juda mehribon edi.
That's the house where my grandfather lived.
Who's the man you were talking to?
I didn't like the film we watched yesterday.
mi: The book I read it was good.
The book I read was good.
The hotel we stayed was nice.
The hotel we stayed at was nice.
The town which I was born
The town where I was born
The man called me is here.
The man who called me is here.
